jobs.title: Sr. Manager, Pricing and Deal Desk
jobs.excerpt: KLDiscovery is a global leader in eDiscovery, information governance, and data recovery, helping law firms, corporations, and government agencies solve complex data challenges.
jobs.description:
KLDiscovery is a global leader in eDiscovery, information governance, and data recovery, helping law firms, corporations, and government agencies solve complex data challenges. We partner with clients across the full data lifecycle — from forensic collection through legal review, production, and managed hosting — spanning services, managed services/SaaS (Nebula), and support.

The Role

KLDiscovery is seeking a Senior Manager, Pricing & Deal Desk to own how we price, structure, and govern every complex deal across services, SaaS, and hybrid offerings. This is a gatekeeper role, not a modeling-support role: this person sits at the intersection of FP&A, Revenue Operations, Sales, and the Executive Leadership Team, and is accountable for deal integrity from quote to close.

Pricing strategy at KLDiscovery is set collectively — through a Pricing Council/Steerco this role runs and staffs with input from FP&A, Rev Ops, Sales, and Marketing leadership. This role owns the mechanics, governance, data, and AI-driven tooling that make that strategy executable and enforceable — they are the operator and analytical backbone of the council, not a sole decision-maker on strategy.

This is an AI-native role. The expectation is not manual spreadsheet-building — it is designing and running AI-assisted pricing models, scenario/Monte Carlo simulations, and automated review workflows (in the vein of AI-assisted Excel work already in use elsewhere in the business, e.g. Nebula ECA), so the team's analytical capacity scales without scaling headcount. This role comes with an expected annual basic salary of $160,000 - 170,000.

What You'll Do

Own the Deal Desk & Approval Governance

  • Serve as the single gatekeeper for non-standard pricing, discounting, and complex deal structures before they go to Legal/Finance sign-off.

  • Design and enforce approval workflows and escalation tiers (standard terms vs. exception vs. ELT-level approval), modeled on the same discipline already applied to sales-split and closed-deal controls.

  • Ensure no deal closes with unpriced or unlogged concessions — including waived/free services (e.g., training credits) — so every giveaway is captured as a $0 promotional credit rather than invisible margin leakage.

Run Pricing Governance & the Pricing Council

  • Own the operating cadence of the cross-functional Pricing Council (FP&A, Rev Ops, Sales, Marketing, ELT stakeholders), including agenda, data package, and follow-through on action items.

  • Translate Council direction into documented pricing policy, discounting guardrails, and approval matrices — this role executes and enforces strategy set collectively, not in isolation.

  • Maintain one consistent view of pricing across the full portfolio — services, managed services/SaaS, and support — so no offering is priced in a silo.

AI-Native Pricing Analytics & Modeling

  • Build AI-assisted pricing tools, not manual models: scenario tools, calculators, and Monte Carlo-style simulations run through AI-assisted platforms, with the analyst validating and interpreting output rather than hand-building every calculation.

  • Automate recurring analyses (margin/discount trend tracking, deal-outcome pattern detection) so cycle time drops and consistency improves.

  • Bring enough modeling fluency to build, validate, and challenge AI-generated outputs — the bar is analytical judgment and structuring, not manual Excel throughput.

Protect Margin on Complex Deal Structures

  • Partner with Sales and Delivery on strategic and structurally complex deals (e.g., platform transitions, dual-hosting/dual-cost scenarios, Second Request work) to catch cost exposure before contracts sign — not after.

  • Flag and quantify hidden cost overlap (e.g., concurrent third-party licensing and proprietary platform hosting during a client transition) as part of deal review, not as a post-close finance discovery.

  • Distinguish revenue-driven pricing actions from structural/cost-side changes for downstream QoE and credit-agreement addback purposes, in partnership with FP&A.

Systems, Data & Reporting Integrity

  • Own pricing/quote data hygiene in SFDC/CPQ — no deal desk decision should run on a hardcoded or unvalidated number.

  • Ensure every priced deal is tagged correctly to the segment/SKU structure (L1/L2/L3 revenue reporting framework) so pricing outcomes roll up cleanly to board and lender reporting.

  • Build and maintain KPI reporting on margin, discounting variability, deal velocity, and Council-adopted tooling.

What You Bring

  • 8–10+ years in pricing, deal desk, revenue operations, or commercial finance — ideally with direct P&L or margin accountability, not purely support/analyst experience.

  • Demonstrated ability to run governance: designing approval workflows, chairing cross-functional forums, and holding Sales accountable to process.

  • Comfort using AI-assisted analytics tools to build and scale pricing models (Excel fluency is expected as a baseline for validating outputs, not the primary skill being hired for).

  • Experience supporting complex B2B deals — services, SaaS, or legal tech preferred — including multi-platform or transition-period pricing.

  • Executive presence: this role will present to ELT and needs to hold their own in that room, not just produce the analysis behind it.

  • Strong cross-functional influence — this role has no direct reports over Sales or Delivery but must drive discipline across both.

Preferred

  • Experience in eDiscovery, legal tech, or managed/usage-based services pricing.

  • Direct experience with AI-assisted modeling tools (e.g., Claude, Copilot) for scenario or simulation work, not just traditional BI tools.

  • Experience with Salesforce, CPQ, or deal-desk workflow tooling.

  • Familiarity with QoE/credit-agreement addback treatment and covenant-relevant reporting.

Success Metrics

  • Reduction in unpriced/unlogged concessions and margin leakage on complex or transitional deals.

  • Deal desk cycle time and reduction in discounting variability.

  • Adoption and effectiveness of AI-assisted pricing tools (measured reduction in manual model-build time).

  • Clean, audit-ready pricing data flowing into segment/SKU and lender-facing reporting with no manual bridges.

  • Pricing Council cadence held consistently, with documented decisions and follow-through.

Equal Opportunity Statement

KLDiscovery is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive team.

jobs.description:
Fiji Program Support Platform (FPSP)

  • Short Term Personnel (40 working input days)
  • Remote – home based with travel to Suva, Fiji
  • Open to both National and International Applicants

  • Please apply online by submitting a cover letter addressing how you meet the selection criteria of this role and up-to-date comprehensive CV

Program Overview:

The Fiji Program Support Platform (FPSP or the ‘Platform’) is a Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) investment that contributes to the delivery of Fiji’s national development priorities, in line with the Australia’s International Development Policy, the Fiji-Australia Vuvale Partnership and the Development Partnership Plan.

The Platform delivers key bilateral programs, such as health, education, scholarships, social infrastructure, governance, climate and emergency preparedness and response. Platform activities identify and address climate risks, promote climate action, and gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) across and beyond the sector programs.

The Platform has three functional Outcomes:

  1. The Platform has delivered its sector program outcomes, including through supporting strategic coherence, planning, partnerships management, data and learning across the portfolio of investments.
  2. The Platform has prioritised gender equality, disability-inclusive development, and climate and disaster resilience, in its systems and practices. This includes in how it undertakes sector programming and its engagement with selected Government of Fiji (GoF) agencies.
  3. The Platform administers timely and efficient programming that is: value for money; maximises use of local supply chains; and supports good governance, and public diplomacy, effective decision making and risk management.

AFEP Overview:

The Australian Government is supporting Fiji’s education sector through the Australia Fiji Education Program (AFEP, the Program) working with the Ministry of Education (MoE).

The objective of the AFEP is “to work with the Government of Fiji under the Vuvale Partnership to catalyse quality education delivery for all Fijian children”.

The changes expected by the end of the five-year program are:

  • EOPO 1: Schools, particularly trial schools, have improved student literacy and numeracy outcomes, supported by enabling policies, plans and data from the Ministry of Education.
  • EOPO 2: Heads of schools and teachers, supported by enabling policies and data from the Ministry of Education, provide a safe, resilient and inclusive learning environment for all students, particularly in trial schools.

Four intermediate outcomes will provide pathways to meet these end of program outcomes in priority areas, like implementation of the revised literacy and numeracy curriculum in primary and secondary schools, professional development interventions, analysis and improvement of the Fiji Education Management Information System (FEMIS), as well as GEDSI and student wellbeing.

The funding for the program is approximately AUD45 million over 9 years (5 years, with an option to extend for a further 4 years) and delivered through a range of activities to achieve the program’s objectives. Implementation modalities include technical advice, procurement of technical services and goods, minor works and infrastructure upgrades, capacity building and training support, support to Ministry led initiatives and innovations, and grants to civil society organisations (CSOs).

Position Summary:

AFEP is seeking an experienced Numeracy Curriculum Specialist to support an evidence-informed review and critical appraisal of Fiji’s primary numeracy curriculum. The consultant will build targeted TTIs and MoE capability to undertake evidence-informed curriculum review while providing specialist technical advice on primary numeracy curriculum quality and implementation.

The specialist will guide and support selected TTIs to apply an appropriate curriculum review framework (or combination of recognised frameworks) and draw on a broad body of numeracy research to assess how well the curriculum reflects contemporary evidence on early numeracy development, Fiji’s linguistic and cultural context and the realities of classroom implementation. The review is not intended to validate or promote any single instructional model.

The specialist will guide and support selected TTIs to provide options and/or recommendations emerging from the analysis, which will be evidence-based, feasible in Fiji’s context and respectful of existing work and national priorities.

Key Responsibilities:

The specialist will advise, guide and support a selected TTIs curriculum team to carry-out the following:

Task 1: Curriculum Review and Analysis

  • Develop an appropriate curriculum review framework, building upon existing recognised review frameworks, to structure the appraisal of Fiji’s primary numeracy curriculum, ensuring methodology is transparent, evidence-informed and suited to Fiji’s context.
  • Review the primary numeracy curriculum (Years 1–4), including syllabi, teacher guides, scope and sequence, instructional expectations, pacing and assessment guidance to determine coherence and developmental and contextual appropriateness.
  • Analyse how the curriculum sequences and integrates key components of early numeracy development, including number sense, operations, mental maths, mathematical reasoning, problem solving, measurement, geometry, patterns, data and mathematical language and assess whether the progression supports students’ development in ways that are realistic and appropriate for Fiji’s linguistic, cultural and classroom contexts.
  • Consider impact of contextual factors including but not limited to class size, language of instruction, teacher foundational knowledge and skill set, resource availability - particularly the availability and diversity of numeracy teaching and learning materials across a developmental progression, including concrete manipulatives, teaching aids and broader school-level realities.
  • Examine existing assessment tools and expected learning outcomes vis-à-vis the existing numeracy curriculum within the context of current learning progression and teacher capacity to utilise them
  • Review available data such as PILNA, Fiji national assessment data, classroom observation evidence, teacher competency evidence.

Task 2: Evidence-Informed Guidance

  • Draw on a broad base of mathematics education research and evidence, including studies on foundational numeracy development, mathematics mastery approaches, problem solving and reasoning, formative assessment practices, multilingual and culturally responsive mathematics education and classroom-based evidence from comparable contexts, to inform the analysis.
  • Provide suggestions where appropriate on ways the curriculum could be strengthened to better support numeracy learning and achievement considering Fiji’s multilingual context, teacher capacity, available teaching and learning resources, assessment tools and system level implementation realities.
  • Offer guidance on realistic and context-appropriate approaches to developing foundational numeracy skills, number sense, mathematical reasoning, problem solving, conceptual understanding, ensuring they are feasible within Fiji’s instructional environment and support learning progression across the primary years.
  • Consider the extent to which the curriculum promotes a coherent progression of mathematical concepts and skills, ensuring that foundational understandings are established before more complex ideas are introduced and that learning builds cumulatively across year levels
  • Provide advice on strategies that support equitable numeracy outcomes for all learners, including students learning in multilingual settings, students requiring additional learning support, and those in rural and remote communities.

Task 3: Teaching Quality, Assessment & System Considerations

Identify and document existing GEDSI and CDR considerations. Ensure that all outputs: promote equity and inclusion, including gender-responsive approaches; address the needs of diverse and disabled learners, including students in remote and underserved areas; reflect principles of effective teaching and learning under resource constraints; align with evidence-based international best practices in mathematics education; and, incorporate climate disaster resilience (CDR) subject matter and how mathematics supports CDR

Task 4: Classroom Resourcing

  • Conduct a structured review of curriculum-aligned teaching and learning resources including mathematics textbooks, teacher guides, teaching aids and manipulatives, assessment tools, and supplementary materials, assessing their sufficiency, quality, progression, accessibility and alignment with curriculum expectations.
  • Assess whether resources adequately support differentiated instruction and inclusive learning practices, including for students learning in multilingual contexts, students requiring additional support, and learners in rural and remote settings.
  • Work with the AFEP team to utilise, and where needed support the collation of, classroom-level inventories and resource audits, noting that these will be primarily undertaken by AFEP staff.
  • Identify priority gaps in teaching and learning resources and provide practical recommendations for strengthening the quality, accessibility, and effective use of curriculum-aligned numeracy resources across schools, considering teacher capacity, implementation feasibility and resource availability.

Task 5: Consultation and Dialogue

  • Engage constructively with selected TTIs, MoE curriculum teams, teachers, heads of schools and other stakeholders to validate findings and ensure relevance and practicality of recommendations.
  • Facilitate discussions on options without prescribing a single solution, supporting MoE to weigh evidence, feasibility and priorities.

Task 6: Recommendations

  • Support the co-design of evidence-based recommendations and next steps with MoE and selected TTIs.
  • Potential areas for consideration depending on findings, may include but are not limited to the following:
  1. enhancing alignment between curriculum intentions and instructional expectations
  2. strengthening the coherence and alignment of formative and summative assessment approaches
  3. strengthening links between the primary mathematics curriculum and pre-service teacher preparation
  4. Identifying priorities for teacher professional development – pre- and in-service

Key Deliverables:

  • #

    Deliverable

    Description

    Indicative days

    1

    Inception Brief (2-3 pages)

    Outlines proposed approach post or prior to engagement with TTI, subject to advancement of TTI team formation, including:

    • Options for the curriculum review framework(s) and/or response to the TTI proposed methodology with recommendations where required

    • School/classroom visit plan and expected activities

    • analytical lenses and methods.

    • document/data/key informant requirements.

    • confirmed workplan and timelines.

    5

    2

    Curriculum Diagnostic Review (10–12 pages)

    Evidence-informed analysis from field work of the curriculum’s strengths, gaps and areas for clarification or refinement based on the agreed framework(s). Includes discussion of contextual factors, system alignment and implications of feasibility. The Review Paper will be co-developed with the TTIO Review team.

    18

    3

    Options and Recommendations Paper (10 – 15 pages)

    Presentation of a set of evidence-based options for MoE and selected TTIs reflecting pathways for curriculum refinement. Clear recommendations, implications for teacher development and requirements relating to materials, guidance, or system supports. The Recommendations Paper will be co-developed with the TTI Review team.

    10

    4

    Presentation and Validation Session

    Support to TTU for a slide deck summarising key findings, options and recommendations; dialogue with MoE/TTI Review team to confirm accuracy, relevance and next steps. Light touch exit presentation and update for AFEP and DFAT.

    2

    5

    Final report (consolidated)

    In collaboration with the TTI Review team, submission of a final consolidated report that integrates the Curriculum Diagnostic Review and an Options & Recommendations Paper. The Final Report will incorporate feedback from MoE, AFEP and other stakeholders following the validation session.

    5

    Total:

    40

Key Working Relationships :

The consultant will work under the direction of the AFEP Team Lead or delegate and collaborate with:

  • Selected Teacher Training Institutions School of Education
  • MoE Curriculum Advisory Services team
  • AFEP technical specialists (Teaching & Learning, MEL, GEDSI)
  • Other stakeholders as identified by MoE or AFEP

Selection Criteria:

The Advisor should have the following qualifications/experience

  • Advanced degree in mathematics education, curriculum studies or related field
  • Experience in primary mathematics curriculum development, review and/or reform
  • Experience in teacher education ideally with demonstrable formative maths experience
  • Experience carrying out national teacher needs analysis
  • Experience in developing country, contexts
  • Experience working within multilingual education environments
  • Strong facilitation, consultation, and analytical skills.
  • High-level written and verbal communication and ability to produce clear, policy-relevant outputs.
  • Experience in Pacific and/or Small Island contexts and/or comparable education systems (desirable)

How to Apply:

Applications close on 7 October 2026.

Please apply online by submitting a cover letter addressing how you meet the selection criteria for this role and up-to-date comprehensive CV.

Job Summary

Job Summary:

Location: 100% remote (US only), supporting VA medical centers in VISN 7 Pay: 25.00/hr-30.00/hr · Term: 12-month base period plus four 12-month option periods

About the role

Aptive Resources is hiring experienced inpatient coders to support the Health Information Management Service (HIMS) at Veterans Affairs medical centers across Georgia, Alabama, and South Carolina. You'll code inpatient admissions for Veterans from home, using the VA's electronic health record. The VA expects about 15,000 inpatient episodes a year across the Atlanta, Birmingham, Augusta, Charleston, and Central Alabama facilities.

Primary Responsibilities

What you'll do

  • Review inpatient records in CPRS and assign accurate ICD-10-CM and ICD-10-PCS codes and DRGs.
  • Complete Patient Treatment File (PTF) transactions (101, 401, 501, 601, 701/702, and 801) according to VHA Handbook 1907.03 and 1907.04.
  • Abstract the required data and enter it in VistA through the VA-approved encoder.
  • Decide whether an episode is billable, and record the reason when it isn't (for example, care for a service-connected condition or Agent Orange exposure).
  • Code according to the Cooperating Parties' guidelines, AHA Coding Clinic, and the VHA Handbook for Coding Guidelines. VHA guidance takes priority when they conflict.
  • Exclude symptoms that are part of a confirmed diagnosis, and findings that don't affect current care.
  • Send questions about conflicting, unclear, or incomplete documentation to your supervisor.
  • Re-review your coded records when the VA questions them before billing or after a claim is denied, then correct the codes or back them up with coding references.
  • Maintain at least 95% accuracy and meet each facility's turnaround times.

Minimum Qualifications

Required qualifications

  • An active RHIA, RHIT, CCS, or CPC-H credential. CCS is preferred for this role.
  • At least 2 years of recent inpatient facility coding experience, including ICD-10-PCS and DRG assignment.
  • Completion of an accredited coding, HIM, or health information technician program.
  • Formal training in anatomy and physiology, medical terminology, pathophysiology, pharmacology, and reimbursement methods.
  • Proficiency with an industry-standard encoder, such as 3M or Optum.
  • US citizenship, and the ability to pass a federal background investigation (NACI) and fingerprinting.
  • A private, secure home workspace with reliable high-speed internet.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with VA systems, including VistA, CPRS, and the PTF.
  • Experience coding for an acute care hospital or academic medical center.
  • Experience with CDI queries or responding to claim denials.

Additional requirements

  • Complete the VA's annual Privacy and Information Security Awareness and HIPAA training (TMS 10176 and 10203) before starting, and once a year after that.
  • Follow AHIMA's Standards of Ethical Coding and VA confidentiality rules.
  • Aptive provides the laptop, encoder, and reference materials.

About Aptive

Arrow ARC supports Veterans Health Administration facilities and offices across the U.S. with health care staffing and program support via the 10-year Integrated Critical Staffing Program (ICSP). We provide staffing solutions to address critical shortages in VHA medical facilities caused by turnover, recruitment issues, seasonal needs, surges or emergencies.

Arrow is a certified Service-Disabled, Veteran-Owned Small Business joint venture between Artemis ARC and Aptive Resources, two award-winning companies that share an agile, mission-focused, results driven approach in the federal sector.​ Arrow provides management consulting services and specializes in working with federal government agencies like the Department of Veterans Affairs and Office of Personnel Management.​

  • Build and maintain security guardrails using AWS-native services (IAM, GuardDuty, Security Hub, Config, CloudTrail, KMS, WAF, Macie, Inspector)
  • Implement and manage Infrastructure as Code security controls (Terraform/CloudFormation) with policy as code
  • Support System Security Plans (SSPs), ATO activities, and POA&M remediation
  • Perform continuous monitoring, vulnerability scanning, patch management tracking, and monthly/annual assessment support

Overview

SSOE is seeking a strategic and business-minded Vice President & General Counsel to serve as the company’s chief legal advisor. This role provides enterprise-wide legal leadership, guiding risk management, contract strategy, regulatory compliance, and corporate governance across domestic and international operations. The General Counsel partners closely with senior leadership to enable informed decision-making, support growth initiatives, and protect the organization’s interests, while fostering a proactive, solutions-oriented legal approach aligned with SSOE’s mission and values.

AI and Innovation

At SSOE, we don’t just talk about the future, we build it. As a leader in industry AI adoption, we empower our team to work smarter by providing responsible access to the industry leading AI Large Language Models, vibe-coding platforms, and securely integrating advanced tools into every role. From day one, you’ll receive the training and support needed to leverage AI as a core tool for enhancing productivity, sparking creativity, and streamlining complex workflows.

Responsibilities

The following duties are typical of the position but are not all encompassing. Responsibilities include those required to deliver quality service on schedule and within budget in a team environment.

Legal Strategy & Leadership:

  • Serve as the Company’s lead in-house attorney and trusted advisor to the C-Suite, Executive Management Team, and Board of Directors.
  • Provide proactive, business-oriented legal advice on risk, strategy, and operations across the enterprise.
  • Support Board governance activities and may serve as Corporate Secretary or Assistant Secretary, as designated.
  • Develop and maintain a proactive, strategic, practical, risk-based legal framework that supports the Company’s domestic and international operations.
  • Manage and oversee outside counsel relationships, including selection, budgeting, and performance.
  • Develop and maintain international legal partnerships to position SSOE to adhere to international laws and regulations.
  • Promote a proactive legal posture focused on risk mitigation rather than reactive issue management.

Contract Management:

  • In conjunction with Contract Manager, oversee the drafting, review, and negotiation of contracts, including client agreements, subconsultant agreements, joint ventures, NDAs, and vendor agreements. Serve as first level escalation advisor.
  • Provide guidance on contract risk allocation, including limitation of liability, indemnification, insurance, dispute resolution, and standard of care provisions.
  • Partner with operations to guide in proper contract language.
  • Develop and maintain contract templates, standards, and playbooks to improve consistency and efficiency.
  • Advise project teams and leadership on contractual risk and business implications of key terms.
  • Support and lead legal aspects of mergers, acquisitions, and other strategic transactions, including due diligence and agreement negotiation.

Claims, Disputes & Litigation:

  • Oversee claims management and dispute resolution strategies, including early risk assessment and resolution planning.
  • Manage litigation, arbitration, and mediation matters in coordination with outside counsel.
  • Partner with internal stakeholders and insurers on claims, coverage, and dispute-related matters.
  • Develop processes and training to reduce claims exposure and improve project-level risk management.

Regulatory Compliance & Risk Management:

  • Monitor and ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, local, and international laws and regulations.
  • Support enterprise risk management initiatives, including contractual, operational, and regulatory risks.
  • Partner with Finance on insurance matters, including claims and renewals.
  • Provide legal oversight related to data privacy, AI use, confidentiality, and other emerging risks.
  • Provide legal support for Stock Program
  • Oversee all state and local licensure applications, renewals
  • Oversee all state and local business filings and renewals
  • Stay current on legal/litigation/insurance issues relevant to the AEC industry

Employment Practices (in partnership with SVP, People & Culture):

  • Provide legal counsel on employment-related matters, including policies, investigations, and risk mitigation.
  • Advise on hiring, discipline, termination, and workforce-related legal issues.
  • Support compliance with employment laws and regulations across jurisdictions.
  • Coordinate with outside counsel on employment disputes and claims, as needed.
  • Partner with Learning & Development to train leaders on contract management and risk mitigation topics.

Organization and People Leadership:

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Operations, Finance, Risk Management, and People & Culture.
  • Support development of internal legal processes, tools, and training programs (including use of technology and AI where appropriate).
  • Provide leadership and direction to legal support resources (e.g., paralegal, contract administration).
  • Maintain strong relationships with external legal partners and industry organizations.
  • Lead by example in alignment with the Company’s Mission, Vision, and Values.
  • Domestic and international travel may be required.

Qualifications

What You Will Bring

  • Juris Doctorate (JD) from an accredited law school and licensed to practice law in the State of Ohio.
  • Minimum 10-15 years of relevant legal experience, including significant experience in professional design contracting, commercial/construction contracting, dispute resolution/litigation management, advice and counseling, and corporate transactions.
  • Experience in the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry strongly preferred.

What We Will Bring

  • Competitive Salary: $220k - $260k/year depending on education and experience.
  • Bonus and Incentives: Eligibility for our annual discretionary bonus based on company and individual performance and goals,
  • Comprehensive Benefits: Health, dental, and vision insurance, life insurance, 401K retirement savings plan (with company matching), professional development and training, generous PTO, and paid holidays.
  • Hybrid or Full Time Remote Work Schedule option for this role, providing you with the flexibility to achieve work-life balance while excelling in your career.

Why SSOE?

  • Ranked Leader: We are a Great Place to Work for 9 consecutive years.
  • Innovative Culture: We lead the AEC industry in AI integration, Lean practices, and project delivery technology.
  • Professional Growth: Join a firm where you have the freedom to shape your own career path while supporting some of the most visionary projects in the country.

At FUJIFILM Holdings America Corporation, we’re redefining innovation across the industries we touch—from healthcare and photography to semiconductors and data storage. With roots in photosensitive materials and a legacy of groundbreaking technology, we now lead 23 diverse affiliate businesses across the Americas.

At Fujifilm you’ll have the opportunity to explore and grow your skills in new, exciting ways. Employee Communications

  • Develop and execute integrated employee communication strategies aligned with business objectives, Corporate Communications Strategy, company culture, and organizational priorities.

  • Create and manage communications across multiple channels, including email, intranet, digital platforms, employee meetings, town halls, videos, newsletters, presentations, and leadership communications.

Content & Storytelling

  • Identify employee and community stories that can be leveraged across internal and external channels within FUJIFILM Americas, as well as amplified globally.
  • Ensure communications are consistent with the company’s brand, voice, tone, and communication standards.

Overview

This position is responsible for protecting Bio-Rad’s data and cloud estate and for leading high-severity security incident response outside US hours. The role owns the enterprise Data Loss Prevention (DLP) program, responsible for cloud security (AWS and Azure), and acts as the senior escalation point for security alerts in the non-US time zone. The ideal candidate will have a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security or a closely related subject; an advanced degree is preferred. The position requires strong collaboration skills and the ability to work effectively with IT infrastructure, application teams, business users and managed security service providers.

This position is responsible for protecting Bio-Rad’s data and cloud estate and for leading high-severity security incident response outside US hours. The role owns the enterprise Data Loss Prevention (DLP) program, responsible for cloud security (AWS and Azure), and acts as the senior escalation point for security alerts in the non-US time zone. The ideal candidate will have a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security or a closely related subject; an advanced degree is preferred. ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Support Azure cloud security engineering work, including Microsoft Graph API automation, secure configuration, and identity and workload hardening.
  • Serve as the security alert lead contact for the non-US time zone for all High and Critical cases, owning end-to-end handling of complex and high-risk incidents through documented closure within SLA.
  • Increase L2 support team’s effectiveness through standardized SOPs, expert guidance, structured escalation support and automation playbooks that shift work left to L2 and reduce escalation volume.
  • Act as integration owner and backup contact for the 3rd party managed detection and response service.
  • Ensure Information Security operations remain compliant with ISO 27001, data privacy regulations and other applicable requirements; support internal audit, FedRAMP and Legal requests.
  • Support Information Security special projects and act as designated backup across key security and GIT domains, building T-shaped skills across the function.
  • Prepare reports, technical presentations and KPI/metrics reporting for management decision-making

Snapshot of the Candidate’s Day: (Describe in a short paragraph, what a day in the life of this role might look like)

  • Reviewing and monitoring security logs for our networks and cloud infrastructure to identify and investigate any potential security threats or vulnerabilities.
  • DLP program – reviewing what the system blocked, tuning policies, and working through exception requests from the business
  • Communicating specific security needs and recommending appropriate security measures.
  • Reviewiong configuration of security tools such as firewalls, intrusion detection systems, and encryption technologies to protect our networks and data.

What the Candidate Brings: (Top 5 required attributes, skills, and work experience)

  • Deep, hands-on data protection experience – enterprise DLP policy design, tuning and exception management, plus data classification and labeling, ideally with Microsoft Purview.
  • Strong Azure cloud security skills – assessment, secure configuration, identity and workload protection, remediation at scale, and automation via Graph API and scripting.
  • Proven incident response leadership at L2 support team with an MSSP or 24x7 SOC, owning High and Critical cases end to end.
  • Excellent judgment and communication – able to explain risk and trade-offs to Legal, business stakeholders and executives, and to write SOPs that others can follow.

  • Hands-on incident response experience at L2/L3, including ownership of High and Critical cases through closure alongside an MSSP or 24x7 SOC partner, and authorship of SOPs, runbooks and automation/SOAR playbooks. Incident report writing skills.

jobs.title: Director, Product Marketing
jobs.excerpt: OverviewRachio is looking for a Director of Product Marketing to own how Rachio decides what to build, how we position it, and how we bring it to market across hardware, software, and subscriptions.
jobs.description:
Overview

Rachio is looking for a Director of Product Marketing to own how Rachio decides what to build, how we position it, and how we bring it to market across hardware, software, and subscriptions. This is a senior leader role at Rachio and the owner of our go-to-market (GTM) processes: the mechanism that takes an idea from concept through business case, launch, and post-launch iteration, and helps to surface key debates and to align cross functional teams (across Product, Engineering, Supply Chain, Sales, Support, and Marketing) to a shared set of goals.

The scope spans smart lighting, smart sprinkler and hose controllers, partner and OEM products, and the software and subscription experiences that sit on top of them. It's inherently cross-functional and inherently commercial: you are measured on adoption, revenue, and channel performance, not on the volume of collateral produced. The right person is equally comfortable running a customer research plan, writing a pricing and positioning narrative for the exec team, and sitting in a firmware trade-off conversation with engineering to understand what a feature actually does before deciding how to sell it.

A note on how this role works. Rachio runs a flat organization that maintains a high ownership and fast paced start-up culture. As such, this is a senior individual contributor role. Your influence comes from the quality of your thinking, the clarity of your writing, and your credibility with the people who own the functions you depend on - not from headcount. It has large ownership and depends on your ability to form clear, concise data-driven strategies that earn trust on the team and drive decisions. If you're looking for a role where you set direction and a team executes it, this isn't that role. If you want the leverage of shaping a category-leading portfolio without the overhead of a large org, it is.

Responsibilities

Own the GTM process

  • Build and run the end-to-end GTM process that moves opportunities from ideation to in-market execution, including setting the strategy, collecting feedback, sizing of opportunities, determining key debates and decisions with clear business cases, stage gates, launch readiness, and post-launch review.
  • Set the strategic goals and success criteria for each initiative up front, and drive alignment on them across Product, Engineering, Finance, Operations, Sales, Support, Marketing, and others.
  • Own launch readiness as a mechanism, not a meeting: clear owners, clear dates, clear go/no-go criteria, and an honest retro afterward.
  • Identify where the process itself is the bottleneck and fix it. This role is expected to build repeatable GTM motions and systems that can scale your work across teams.

Be the senior product marketing voice in roadmap and product development

  • Partner with Product Management to shape the roadmap that’s led with data: market sizing, customer research, competitive intelligence, channel input, and knowledgeable ways to leverage AI to organize the data into tangible next steps.
  • Maintain a working understanding of the market: competitive lineups, adjacent smart home platforms and protocols, pro channel dynamics, and where the category is heading.

Positioning, messaging, and pricing

  • Define positioning and messaging architecture for hardware, software, and subscription offerings, and translate technical capability into language customers and pros actually use.
  • Own the single source of truth for each product: positioning, claims, feature availability, competitive comparisons, FAQs, and objection handling.
  • Develop pricing and packaging recommendations in partnership with Product, Sales, and Marketing: good/better/best structures, subscription tiers, channel-specific SKUs, promotional strategy. Each should include financial modeling to support the recommendations.

Launch and channel execution

  • Lead integrated launches across the professional channel, retail, and D2C.
  • Build the enablement that makes the channel effective: support of pro training, distributor and rep materials, retail line reviews, packaging and shelf messaging, product spec and comparison tools.
  • Partner with the Brand Studio and Marketing team to translate positioning into campaigns and measure what they return.
  • Action and close the post-launch feedback loops: what's confusing customers, what's driving returns, what priorities we need to improve CSAT.
  • Lead international expansion opportunities with agency and contractor support where it makes sense.
  • How to size new country expansion and how to build brand awareness in these regions with targeted customer segments.

Voice of the customer and measurement

  • Own the customer research agenda across homeowners and professional installers: qualitative and quantitative, primary and syndicated.
  • Instrument launches so success is measurable: adoption, attach and activation rates, sell-through, ASP, retention, NPS.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of product marketing, GTM, or closely related commercial experience, including significant time owning initiatives end-to-end.
  • Comfort operating as a hands-on individual contributor. You write the narrative and docs, build the model, and run the launch yourself rather than assigning it.
  • Demonstrated ownership of a full product lifecycle from concept through launch and iteration, with results you can speak to specifically.
  • Experience marketing connected hardware, consumer electronics, IoT, or technical products, including the realities of long hardware lead times, supply constraints, certification, and channel timing.
  • Experience marketing software or subscription offerings: adoption, attach, retention, and monetization.
  • Track record of driving direction and alignment across product, engineering, finance, operations, and sales without owning those functions.
  • Strong analytical foundation: comfortable building the model, working in spreadsheets and BI tools, and defending the assumptions.
  • Exceptional written communication. Distill a complex set of decisions into a written narrative a leadership team can act on.
  • Bachelor's degree.
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States.

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Experience building GTM or NPI processes from scratch, or materially rebuilding one that wasn't working.
  • Experience in two-step distribution or professional trade channels (irrigation, landscape, electrical, HVAC, plumbing, building products) alongside retail and D2C.
  • Experience with smart home platforms and protocols: Matter, Thread, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and have enough technical fluency to be useful in engineering conversations.
  • Experience with outdoor products, lighting, water management, or the sustainability categories.
  • Experience with partner, OEM, or co-marketing programs.
  • MBA or advanced degree.

Salary range for candidates based in California: $248,000 - $372,000

Salary range for candidates based in Colorado - New York- New York City or Maryland : $232,000 - $348,000

Salary ranges include base salary and annual incentive bonus if applicable.

Exact compensation may vary based on skills, experience, and location.

Rachio is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.excerpt: OverviewConsilio builds eDiscovery and legal technology solutions used by legal teams at major organizations.
jobs.description:
Overview

Consilio builds eDiscovery and legal technology solutions used by legal teams at major organizations. Our users make consequential decisions inside our products — often under deadline, always under scrutiny. The work is high-stakes by nature: decisions made inside our products carry legal weight.

We're looking for a Lead UX Designer to own design for critical areas of our product suite and to serve as a steward of our design system. Two things make this role unusual. First, you'll be working out how AI shows up inside these workflows. Second, you'll be setting the standards that hold the experience together across a multi-product portfolio, and governing how those standards get used.

This is an individual contributor role. You will set direction, and you'll have real influence over what gets built.

How this role operates

You'll partner with Product and Engineering early — shaping the problem, not styling a decision that's already been made. You'll prototype fast to explore and align, and work with Engineering to keep design and code in sync.

Our internal design team is small and growing. You'll have more ownership than you'd get at a mature design org, and less existing infrastructure to lean on.

Responsibilities

· Own end-to-end design for one or more product areas, from problem framing through delivery and post-launch iteration

· Partner closely with Product and Engineering to shape solutions early, not just execute on requirements

· Translate in-flight product strategy into journeys, information architecture, and interaction patterns

· Define the interaction models for AI-assisted workflows: how users understand what the system did, why it did it, and how far to trust it

· Evolve and maintain Consilio's design system — defining components and patterns, and setting the standards for how they're used

· Build accessibility standards into the system rather than retrofitting it

· Prototype rapidly to explore, align, and de-risk decisions using modern AI tools

· Lead or partner on user research, and turn findings into decisions other people can act on

· Make the case for design decisions and system standards to senior stakeholders through evidence and clear storytelling

Qualifications

· 8+ years designing complex enterprise or B2B software, with shipped work you can walk us through

· Hands-on experience building and maintaining a design system in a multi-product environment — not just consuming one

· Experience designing end-to-end journeys for multi product ecosystems

· Experience with Figma Make, or other similar prompt-based prototyping tools.

· Depth in interaction design, with visual craft strong enough to make the work persuasive

· Demonstrated experience partnering with Product and Engineering from problem definition forward

· Bachelor’s degree in Design (e.g., Interaction, Visual, Industrial Design), HCI, or equivalent practical experience.

Qualities we're looking for

· Systems thinking. You design for scale and consistency by default, not as a cleanup pass.

· Standards judgment. You know when to generalize a pattern and when a one-off is the right answer — and you can say no to a component request without damaging the relationship.

· Comfort with ambiguity. You can make a defensible tradeoff without perfect information, and revisit it when better information arrives.

· Influence without authority. You change what gets built by being persuasive and well-reasoned, not by escalating.

· Clarity under complexity. You can take a genuinely complicated workflow and make it feel obvious.

Portfolio

· Strong portfolio demonstrating complex workflow design across multiple web-based enterprise products.

· Work samples that showcase prototyping ability.

Nice to have

· Experience with AI driven products or designing AI powered interactions

· Formal or self-directed learning in AI/ML concepts

· Prior experience designing for legal, compliance, healthcare, financial services, or another high-consequence regulated domain.

Consilio’s True North Values

  • Client Experience | Listen for the “why”. Clearly define success. Be accountable. Go the extra distance to create moments that matter.
  • Collaboration | Treat everyone with respect. Welcome diverse views. Partner across geography, generations, and teams. Rally around final decisions.
  • Innovation | Always be curious (ABC). Challenge the status quo. Experiment and fail forward. Build for the future.
  • Grit | Focus on what matters. Work with passion and persistence. Think like an owner. Deliver results you’re proud of.

About Us

Join Our Mission

At Omega Technical Services, every role supports a mission that matters. Whether you're advancing national security, driving innovation in nuclear infrastructure, or supporting critical DOE and DoD operations, you’re part of something bigger here.

Overview

Omega Technical Services is seeking an experienced Designer to support Idaho National Laboratory’s Materials and Fuels Complex. The Designer will translate engineering requirements into detailed drawings, 3D parametric models, assemblies, and technical documentation supporting fabrication and installation.

Qualified candidates will have strong PTC Creo proficiency, precision mechanical design expertise, and hands-on experience applying geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T). Candidates with mechanical, electrical, or multidisciplinary design backgrounds who meet these qualifications are encouraged to apply.

Work will be performed remotely, with occasional travel onsite to provide support at MFC as needed.

This position is contingent upon contract award and/or project funding. Candidates may be identified, screened, and submitted prior to award. Employment offers and start dates are dependent upon successful contract award, funding authorization, and client approval.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and revise 2D drawings, 3D parametric models, assemblies, and associated documentation using approved engineering inputs.

  • Prepare drawings that clearly define geometry, interfaces, materials, finishes, processes, tolerances, inspection requirements, and assembly relationships.

  • Apply GD&T in accordance with ASME Y14.5-2009, including datum reference frames, feature control frames, material condition modifiers, and basic dimensions.

  • Evaluate tolerance accumulation and fit at part and assembly interfaces to identify potential fabrication, inspection, assembly, or operational issues.

  • Apply sound parametric modeling practices, including fully constrained sketches, stable design intent, controlled references, and organized assembly structures.

  • Independently check drawings and models for accuracy, completeness, fit, form, function, manufacturability, inspectability, and compliance with applicable standards.

  • Verify bills of material, parts lists, item balloons, quantities, drawing references, notes, weld symbols, and revision information.

  • Maintain drawing and model integrity through established document control, revision control, configuration management, and records processes.

  • Resolve technical review comments and maintain an auditable record of changes.

  • Collaborate with engineers, designers, fabricators, and inspectors to clarify requirements and resolve discrepancies.

  • Manage assigned priorities, provide progress updates, and communicate scope, resource, or schedule concerns.

  • Support backlog reduction and mentor drafting personnel when requested.

  • Perform other duties assigned by the BEA Technical Point of Contact.

Education Requirements

  • Bachelor of Science degree from an accredited institution with at least 5 years of relevant experience; OR at least 10 years of relevant experience without a degree.

jobs.excerpt: ABOUT THE ROLEArgano's Business Consulting practice partners with organizations to design, optimize, and transform how work gets done — connecting strategy to execution by ensuring the people side of change is never an afterthought.
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Argano's Business Consulting practice partners with organizations to design, optimize, and transform how work gets done — connecting strategy to execution by ensuring the people side of change is never an afterthought. As a Lead OCM Consultant, you will own the change management workstream on complex client engagements, leading the strategies, plans, and interventions that drive real adoption and help people move through change successfully.

This is a senior practitioner role — not a project coordinator. You will work directly with executives and senior leaders, coaching them to play their sponsorship roles effectively. You will design and execute stakeholder engagement plans, impact assessments, communications strategies, and training frameworks. You will also serve as a subject matter authority within Argano's community of practice, developing colleagues and contributing to the methodologies that define how we deliver OCM.

Typical engagements include ERP and enterprise technology implementations, operating model redesigns, organizational restructuring, process transformation programs, and post-merger integration — across a range of industries and client environments. You will work across one or more concurrent engagements at any given time.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Engagement Planning & Delivery

▸ Partner with Engagement and Project Managers to translate high-level plans into detailed OCM workplans and inventories of required deliverables — ensuring the change management workstream is integrated, sequenced, and resourced from day one

▸ Apply Argano's LIFT delivery methodology and incorporate key learnings from prior engagements to build change strategies uniquely fitted to each client situation

▸ Establish strong working relationships with client business leaders, project sponsors, and functional stakeholders — building trust that makes OCM work possible

▸ Work across one or more concurrent projects at one or more clients — maintaining quality, pace, and stakeholder confidence throughout

Change Strategy & Stakeholder Engagement

▸ Lead the design and execution of change management strategies and plans that maximize employee adoption, minimize resistance, and accelerate time to proficiency

▸ Conduct change impact assessments across affected roles, processes, systems, and organizational structures — translating findings into targeted intervention plans

▸ Develop and maintain stakeholder analysis and engagement plans — identifying change champions, resistance risks, and influence strategies by group

▸ Help clients understand and articulate the value of investing in the people side of change, including changes to business processes, systems and technology, job roles, and organizational structures

▸ Identify and assess organizational readiness for change throughout the engagement — surfacing risks early and adjusting the plan accordingly

Executive Coaching & Sponsorship

▸ Act as a trusted advisor and coach for senior leaders and executives, helping them understand and fulfill their role as active, visible change sponsors

▸ Prepare leaders to communicate change effectively — providing messaging frameworks, talking points, and facilitation support for key leadership moments

▸ Build leadership alignment and engagement around the change — helping executives model the behaviors the organization needs to see

▸ Navigate organizational politics and resistance at the leadership level with maturity and credibility

Communications

▸ Design and execute end-to-end communications strategies that reach the right audiences with the right message at the right time

▸ Develop communications plans, calendars, and content — from executive announcements to front-line manager briefings to system-user notifications

▸ Write, review, and refine communications across multiple channels — email, town halls, intranet, video, and manager talking points

▸ Measure communication effectiveness and adjust approach based on audience feedback and engagement signals

Training & Enablement

▸ Provide input to the design and development of training strategies, approaches, and programs aligned to the change and the affected audience groups

▸ Define training needs by role and persona — ensuring training content addresses both the 'how' of the new system or process and the 'why' of the change

▸ Support the design, development, and delivery of training programs in collaboration with instructional designers, subject matter experts, and technology teams

▸ Develop or support the development of job aids, quick reference guides, and sustainment tools that support adoption beyond the initial training event

Practice Development & Capability Building

▸ Actively contribute to the development and continuous refinement of Argano's OCM methodologies, tools, templates, and accelerators

▸ Lead and champion a defined set of OCM leading-practice capabilities within the community of practice — teaching and enabling colleagues to deploy them effectively on client engagements

▸ Mentor junior OCM practitioners and analysts through direct project collaboration and structured coaching

Business Development

▸ Build trusted relationships with client leaders that generate expansion opportunities and long-term partnerships

▸ Contribute to proposals and business development pursuits by bringing OCM expertise, scope definition capability, and a track record of measurable adoption outcomes

▸ Participate in thought leadership and knowledge-sharing activities that strengthen Argano's market position in OCM

Travel
Up to 50% travel to client sites, depending on project phase and engagement requirements — typically higher during assessment, design workshops, and go-live support phases

QUALIFICATIONS

Education

▸ Bachelor’s degree preferred; psychology, organizational behavior, communications, business, or HR disciplines are strong fits

▸ Advanced degree (MBA, MS in Organizational Development, I/O Psychology, or related field) is an advantage

▸ Prosci ADKAR certification or equivalent change management certification is strongly preferred

▸ Additional relevant credentials — CCMP, Kotter, LaMarsh, or similar — are valued

Required Experience

▸ 5+ years of hands-on organizational change management experience on complex, enterprise-scale transformation programs

▸ Demonstrated end-to-end OCM delivery capability — from change strategy through stakeholder engagement, communications, training, and sustainment

▸ Proven experience working directly with senior executives as an OCM coach and advisor — not just as a communications or training executor

▸ Solid understanding of how people go through change — the psychology, the resistance patterns, the adoption curve, and what actually moves people from awareness to commitment

▸ Demonstrated ability to build and maintain strong relationships across all levels of an organization, from front-line employees to C-suite executives

▸ Experience on large-scale organizational change efforts — enterprise technology implementations, process transformation, restructuring, or post-merger integration

▸ Strong written and verbal communication skills — ability to craft clear, compelling, audience-appropriate messaging and to present confidently to senior stakeholders

▸ Ability to influence without formal authority, navigate ambiguity, and move diverse groups of stakeholders toward a common goal.

Preferred Experience

▸ Experience delivering OCM on enterprise technology implementations — system agnostic (ERP, HCM, CRM, SCM, or other platforms)

▸ Familiarity with instructional design principles and adult learning theory — ability to contribute meaningfully to training design conversations

▸ Experience with stakeholder analysis and engagement tools, change readiness assessments, and resistance management frameworks

▸ Background working across multiple industries — manufacturing, consumer goods, financial services, life sciences, retail, or public sector preferred

▸ Experience managing or leading a small OCM team or workstream (4+ people)

▸ Comfort working in environments where the OCM methodology needs to be built, not just applied — able to design the approach, not just follow a playbook


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Beyond the qualifications, we are looking for someone who:

▸ Leads with empathy — genuinely understands what it feels like to be on the receiving end of change, and designs interventions with real human experience in mind

▸ Earns credibility fast — can walk into a room of skeptical executives and quickly establish the trust and authority needed to coach effectively

▸ Communicates with precision — knows that the right message, to the right audience, at the right moment is what moves people, and designs every communication with that in mind

▸ Operates as a strategic partner, not a support function — understands the business objectives driving the change and connects OCM activities directly to those outcomes

▸ Is comfortable with ambiguity and resistance — doesn't need perfect conditions to do good work, and doesn't take resistance personally

▸ Develops others — genuinely invested in making junior practitioners better, and in building a stronger OCM practice at Argano

jobs.description:
Responsibilities

Peraton is seeking a UX Analyst to support the DFAS environment by delivering modern, user-centered digital experiences across web and mobile applications.

This is a hands-on UX role focused on moving rapidly from requirements and user needs to high-fidelity, interactive experiences. The UX Analyst will use Figma, AI-assisted design and research tools, design systems, rapid prototyping, usability validation, and accessibility practices to transform complex requirements into intuitive, development-ready solutions.

The ideal candidate is comfortable working directly within Agile product teams and can use AI to accelerate—not replace—UX thinking, research synthesis, design exploration, documentation, accessibility evaluation, and prototyping.

The role requires someone who can take an experience from concept to high-fidelity prototype to development handoff, while collaborating closely with product owners, stakeholders, developers, and end users.

This position is 100% remote.

Responsibilities:

  • Support the full UX lifecycle from discovery, requirements analysis, and user research through high-fidelity design, interactive prototyping, validation, development handoff, and implementation review.
  • Translate business, mission, technical, and user requirements into clear user journeys, task flows, experience maps, information architecture, and interface solutions.
  • Create high-fidelity Figma screens and interactive prototypes that accurately demonstrate intended workflows, interactions, responsive behavior, states, and user outcomes.
  • Use AI-assisted UX workflows to accelerate research synthesis, requirements analysis, concept exploration, content development, accessibility review, prototyping, and design iteration.
  • Apply strong UX judgment to validate and refine AI-generated concepts rather than relying on AI-generated output without human review.
  • Develop and maintain Figma component libraries, variables, reusable patterns, templates, and design-system components that promote consistency and accelerate delivery.
  • Create UX artifacts as appropriate, including user journeys, personas, workflows, information architecture, experience maps, wireframes, high-fidelity mockups, prototypes, storyboards, and design specifications.
  • Conduct and synthesize user research and stakeholder discovery through interviews, surveys, observation, contextual inquiry, usability testing, heuristic evaluations, and other appropriate research methods.
  • Plan, facilitate, and analyze usability testing using interactive prototypes and working applications; translate findings into actionable design recommendations.
  • Rapidly iterate concepts using high-fidelity prototypes and AI-enabled prototyping techniques to allow stakeholders and users to experience proposed solutions before development investment.
  • Design responsive experiences for desktop, tablet, and mobile environments, considering device capabilities, user context, interaction methods, and platform conventions.
  • Ensure designs meet applicable Section 508 and WCAG accessibility requirements, incorporating accessibility into the design process rather than treating compliance as a final review activity.
  • Design accessible interaction patterns including keyboard navigation, focus behavior, semantic structure, form interactions, error handling, color contrast, responsive behavior, and assistive-technology considerations.
  • Apply established organizational design systems and standards, including U.S. Web Design System (USWDS) patterns when applicable.

About SemiAnalysis

SemiAnalysis is an independent research and analysis firm specializing in the Semiconductor and AI industries. We are recognized as the leading authority on the semiconductor supply chain, with the highest concentration of industry experts within one team, and a deep-rooted passion for delving into the intricacies.

We are a global team of analysts, each with extensive networks across the semiconductor supply chain and AI ecosystem, publishing industry shaping articles while participating in numerous conferences annually.

Our newsletters reach more than 200,000 subscribers worldwide, including senior management and c-suite leaders at the leading semiconductor and AI companies.

We also offer three core products:

  • Industry Models – we develop and publish industry models on accelerator shipments, datacentre demand and supply, GPU total cost of ownership, and more. We work with hyperscalers, neoclouds, many of the world’s largest hedge funds, and government agencies.

  • Core Research – our public equity markets product, geared towards financial investors, distils our deep technical research and knowledge into key insights on technology and product trends.

  • Consulting and Technical Due Diligence – We conduct custom research and project work to guide key strategic and investment decisions for the largest private equity funds, leading venture capital firms, companies across the AI ecosystem, and government agencies.


Position Overview

SemiAnalysis is seeking an Economist to connect our proprietary semiconductor, supply chain, and datacenter datasets with the broader macroeconomic picture.

This role will lead the firm’s research on the economics of artificial intelligence, including AI infrastructure investment, productivity growth, labor market effects, economic diffusion, and the contribution of datacenter development to GDP.

The Economist will produce flagship research that informs investors, policymakers, technology companies, and other decision-makers. The ideal candidate combines rigorous economic research, strong quantitative capabilities, and the ability to communicate complex ideas to a broad and sophisticated audience.

Responsibilities

  • Author flagship, long-form research on the macroeconomics of AI, including:

    • AI and datacenter capital expenditure cycles

    • Productivity and economic growth effects

    • GDP contribution from AI infrastructure development

    • Labor market and employment impacts

    • The economics and pace of AI adoption and diffusion

  • Build quantitative models and forecasting infrastructure that translate complex data into actionable economic insights.

  • Develop LLM-driven research and estimation pipelines that convert unstructured information—such as company filings, earnings transcripts, news reports, and planning permits—into structured economic datasets and time series.

  • Translate SemiAnalysis’s bottom-up datasets, including accelerator shipments, datacenter capacity, electricity demand, networking infrastructure, and related supply chain data, into top-down macroeconomic estimates.

  • Conduct econometric analysis and develop forecasts that can be used by investors, corporations, policymakers, and research institutions.

  • Engage with leading academic and policy debates involving:

    • Transformative AI and long-term economic growth

    • AI-driven productivity measurement

    • Explosive growth scenarios

    • Technological diffusion and innovation economics

  • Develop and communicate clear, informed views on where prevailing AI economic frameworks are accurate, incomplete, or incorrect.

  • Represent SemiAnalysis’s economic research and perspectives through client discussions, podcasts, conferences, interviews, and public writing.

  • Work closely with analysts covering semiconductors, datacenters, energy, networking, and AI systems to produce integrated research.

Requirements

  • Bachelors' Degree in Economics or equivalent professional research experience.

  • Strong research background in one or more of the following areas:

    • Macroeconomics

    • Labor economics

    • Innovation economics

    • Productivity

    • Economic growth

    • Industrial organization

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

About the Opportunity

Nemours Radiology is seeking three additional Pediatric Radiologists to join our current overnight group as a 100% remote nighthawk, 1 week on and 2 weeks off model. This position is 100% pediatric imaging, with no fluoroscopy responsibilities, and the provider will be paired with an additional radiologist overnight. Emergency neuroradiology experience is preferred but not required. We offer a competitive salary and generous signing bonus.

Division Highlights

Nemours Radiology is one of the largest pediatric radiology groups in the United States, currently composed of 46 pediatric radiologists, growing to over 50 in 2026, working together to provide state-of-the-art diagnostic and interventional radiology services at our locations in Delaware, Florida, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania. In 2025, we are on track to preform 500,000 imaging examinations across the growing system. The enterprise is integrated within a single PACS, with faculty working from shared worklists, participating in multi-site conferences and initiatives, and sharing after-hours responsibilities including a current dedicated team of 3 nighthawk radiologists. We have collaborative research opportunities supported by dedicated leadership, PhD’s, and a radiology research fellowship. We are also active educationally with Pediatric Radiology and Pediatric Neuroradiology fellowships at our Orlando, FL and Wilmington, DE campuses and radiology residents from multiple programs rotating through the department. Pediatric Radiology fellows are expected to rotate with the nighthawk team during their fellowship year.

Nemours Radiology provides full pediatric imaging services (diagnostic and interventional) for Nemours Children’s Hospital, Delaware, in Wilmington, Nemours Children’s Hospital, Florida, in Orlando, Nemours Children’s Specialty Care in Jacksonville, FL, Nemours Children’s Clinic at Studer Family Children's Hospital at Ascension Sacred Heart in Pensacola, FL, Wolfson Children’s Hospital in Jacksonville, FL as well as several hospital partners for pediatric radiology. Faculty are licensed in all four states and credentialed throughout the system as well as partner institutions. In-house moonlighting is also available.

Academic appointment is available but not required for our emergency radiology section.

  • Comprehensive benefits: health, life, dental, vision

jobs.description:
Overview

The Touro University Graduate School of Social Work is seeking candidates for a full-time (10-month appointment), online, Assistant/Associate Professor in Social Work. The successful candidate must have demonstrated capability to teach in multiple modalities including synchronous (Zoom), and asynchronous online formats. Successful candidates will exhibit a commitment to excellence in teaching, mentoring, instructional design, and engaged scholarship. Experience should include curriculum development, education best practices, instruction/teaching in social work, student advising, ability to engage students both in and out of the classroom. Ideal candidates will have a defined area of research and scholarship and a social work practice area of expertise. Associate-level candidates are expected to demonstrate a sustained record of publications or contributions to an area of expertise. Demonstrated experience with CSWE Accreditation Standards is a plus. A typical workday will entail teaching, advising, and meetings. Faculty carry a 21-credit workload per academic year, with responsibilities distributed across teaching, scholarship, and service. Faculty participate in MSW program activities as needed (orientation, community days, committee meetings, and curriculum development), and will also contribute on departmental and university-wide committees.

The mission of the Touro University Graduate School of Social Work is to educate graduates for clinical social work practice in an urban, and multicultural environment. This is consistent with the general mission of Touro University, which is to provide professional education for the benefit of the individual and society. This general mission is an expression of the Jewish religious tenet of Tikkun Olam, the striving to make the world a better place for all people. In accordance with traditional social work values, the Graduate School of Social Work is committed to providing accessible and affordable quality education to all. The MSW program's educational purpose is to prepare self-reflective professionals who can meet the complex needs of a multitude of populations. The school's curriculum is informed by the person-in-environment, ecological and strengths-based perspectives. The school provides students with a social work education that offers a theoretical and evidence-based foundation in generalist social work, as well as advanced knowledge and skills for effective clinical social work. This education prepares graduates for leadership roles in clinical social work practice with varied populations in the contemporary service delivery environment.

Responsibilities

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Teaching online, asynchronous and synchronous Zoom courses according to workload assignments.
  • Service to the Department, University, and Community Research/Scholarship, including publication, social work academic conferences, funded research.
  • Academic advising for students in the distance education online program option.
  • Participate in standing and ad-hoc committees.
  • Participate in program events, such as orientation and graduation.
  • Build, strengthen, and support community relations.
  • Highly engaged and responsive during stipulated work hours.

Qualifications

Education/Experience

  • Master of Social Work degree and a Doctorate in a related field of study required; a Ph.D. in Social Work or a DSW degree is preferred.
  • Social work licensure preferred A minimum of 3-5 years of graduate-level, teaching experience required.
  • Experience teaching: HBSE, clinical courses preferred.
  • Evidence of research and scholarly activities.
  • Instructional course design experience.
  • Student advising experience.
  • Experience with clinical simulation technology and artificial intelligence experience a plus.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

  • Experience with Canvas and electronic learning management systems.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite including Word, Excel, Power Point, Outlook, Zoom.

Travel

  • Instruction will be fully remote.

Working Conditions

  • Extensive time sitting.
