If you’re looking for a place where your expertise is trusted, your judgment is valued, and your work helps define what’s next for intelligent insurance and retirement technology, Majesco is where that work happens.

Product Owner Director – P&C Commercial Underwriting & AI Innovation

Location: Remote, United States

Help redefine how commercial underwriting works.

Majesco is looking for a senior Property & Casualty (P&C) domain expert who understands commercial underwriting operations and has moved into technology, implementation, or product ownership. This role sits at the intersection of P&C operations expertise, modern insurance platforms, and the next generation of Immersive AI user experience.

You will help translate real operations workflows across policy lifecycle into scalable Majesco agentic capabilities and contribute to the design and execution of AI-powered solutions that improve decision speed, risk insights, and operational efficiency for our customers (insurers and large MGA’s).

This role is ideal for someone who has lived inside P&C underwriting operations, understands the realities of commercial/specialty business, and now wants to shape the technology that will define the next decade of underwriting.

About the Role

Commercial underwriting is rapidly changing.

Carriers are shifting from manual underwriting workflows to AI-assisted decisioning, automated risk assessment, and data-driven underwriting platforms.

As a Senior Business Analyst / Product Owner at Majesco, you will help insurers modernize policy operations on the Majesco P&C platform while also contributing to the design of Agentic AI underwriting capabilities that will power the next generation of underwriting automation.

You will serve as the bridge between commercial underwriting expertise and platform design, ensuring that underwriting and policy workflows, risk evaluation processes, and broker interactions translate into scalable product capabilities.

This role combines P&C underwriting domain leadership, software implementation expertise, and product innovation.

What You Will Do

  • Lead discovery sessions with underwriting leaders, underwriting/policy operations teams, and distribution stakeholders across commercial/specialty P&C lines.
  • Translate real-world P&C underwriting workflows into scalable platform capabilities on the Majesco P&C platform.
  • Design and document underwriting configuration, including risk evaluation rules, underwriting workflows, authority levels, referrals, and decision logic.
  • Guide insurers in implementing underwriting capabilities using a configuration-first approach aligned with Majesco platform standards.
  • Work with product and AI teams to help design the next generation of Agentic AI underwriting tools that assist underwriters in risk selection, triage, and decision support.
  • Help define underwriting data models, risk attributes, and decision signals used to power AI-assisted underwriting workflows.
  • Partner with solution architects and engineering teams to ensure underwriting processes integrate seamlessly with policy administration, rating, distribution portals, and data platforms.
  • Define integration requirements with third-party underwriting data providers such as property data vendors, financial data providers, and risk intelligence platforms.
  • Lead backlog definition, user story development, and acceptance criteria for underwriting platform capabilities in Agile delivery environments.
  • Support testing and validation of underwriting workflows, decision logic, and automated underwriting rules.
  • Mentor business analysts across global teams on P&C underwriting domain knowledge and Majesco implementation best practices.

What You Bring

  • 10 plus years of experience in insurance, insurance technology, or consulting.
  • Deep expertise in Property & Casualty (P&C) insurance, with strong knowledge of commercial underwriting operations.
  • Hands-on experience working in commercial underwriting or underwriting operations before moving into technology, transformation, or implementation roles.
  • Experience implementing or configuring underwriting systems, policy administration systems, or digital underwriting workflows.
  • Strong understanding of commercial underwriting processes, including:
  • Risk triage and submission intake
  • Underwriting evaluation and decision support
  • Referral and authority workflows
  • Broker interactions and underwriting collaboration
  • Policy issuance and endorsement workflows
  • Experience translating underwriting workflows into system capabilities within modern insurance platforms.
  • Experience working in Agile environments using tools such as Jira or Aha!.
  • Ability to work with technical teams to interpret integration patterns, APIs, and data flows.
  • Strong facilitation skills with both underwriting business leaders and engineering teams.

Bonus Points for:

  • Experience working with P&C core platforms, including policy administration or underwriting workbench systems.
  • Exposure to AI-assisted underwriting, decision engines, or underwriting automation platforms.
  • Experience working with underwriting data providers or third-party risk intelligence platforms.
  • Background in commercial and specialty lines, such as:
  • Commercial Package (Property, Liability, Auto, Inland Marie and Excess)
  • Workers Compensation
  • Commercial Auto
  • Specialty lines (Aviation, Marine, etc…)
  • Experience participating in large insurance modernization or platform transformation programs.

Why Join Majesco

Majesco is helping insurers modernize underwriting, policy administration, and digital distribution through cloud platforms and AI-enabled capabilities.

As a member of a rapidly growing and dynamic organization, the successful candidate must be flexible and willing to take on new tasks and responsibilities as business needs evolve. The company reserves the right to vary, change, or update job duties and responsibilities based on business requirements. This role may require shifting priorities, learning new technologies, and contributing to projects outside of the initial scope.

What Majesco Offers:

Majesco is committed to equal pay and transparency. The annual base salary range for this position is $110,000 to $170,000.

Please note that the salary range information provided is a general guideline and combines all of the distinct labor markets within the United States. It is uncommon for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role, and compensation decisions are dependent on a variety of factors. Majesco considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate's work experience, candidate's work location, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, external market data, as well as market and business considerations when making compensation decisions.

At Majesco, we offer a comprehensive employee benefits package with most coverage starting Day One. Our benefits package includes, but is not limited to: Medical, dental & vision insurance; employer-funded HSA coordinating with a high-deductible health plan; FSA, short-term/long-term disability; Life/AD&D insurance; 401(k), flexible time off, paid sick days and 11 paid holidays; paid parental/bonding leave; career anniversary leave and other voluntary benefits.

Job Description: ASP Program Manager

Fluke Health Solutions · Fluke Biomedical Division · Authorized Service Provider (ASP) Program

Reports to: Global Service Sales Leader · Department: Global Service Sales

Job Summary:

The ASP Program Manager owns the day-to-day health, growth, and performance governance of Fluke Health Solutions' global network of Authorized Service Providers (ASPs) — the third-party partners who deliver calibration, repair, and preventive maintenance service on Fluke Biomedical equipment outside of Fluke's direct service footprint.

This role is responsible for the full partner lifecycle: identifying and prioritizing new markets, qualifying and onboarding new ASPs, managing royalty and product-tier authorization structures, and running the ongoing quarterly/annual performance cadence that keeps the existing network reliable, compliant, and financially sound. The role blends program management, partner relationship management, and data-driven decision-making, and is measured on ASP network revenue growth, service quality/SLA compliance, and royalty revenue integrity.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own the ASP performance assessment cadence (quarterly, annual, and trigger-based) as defined in the ASP Assessment Standard Work

  • Evaluate and prioritize new ASP markets using country-level revenue/opportunity modeling (install base, net incremental revenue, cannibalization risk)

  • Score and qualify new ASP candidates against the standard qualification scorecard and Phase 1 audit checklist

  • Manage royalty structure selection and reconciliation across the existing ASP portfolio

  • Own product tier authorization decisions (which service categories each ASP is certified to perform) and reassess at each quarterly review

  • Monitor SLA/turnaround-time performance and loaner pool health across all Tier 2/3 escalations

  • Maintain and report on the ASP KPI dashboard (service volume, revenue vs. plan, customer satisfaction, certification status)

  • Lead or coordinate process-improvement initiatives affecting the ASP network (e.g., contract renewal process, onboarding workflow)

  • Serve as the primary relationship owner for escalated ASP or end-customer issues involving ASP-delivered service

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, Life Sciences, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience

  • 3-5+ years of experience in channel/partner management, service operations, or program management — medical device, biomedical, or technical equipment industry strongly preferred

  • Demonstrated experience managing partner performance against SLAs, KPIs, or contractual scorecards

  • Strong financial/analytical skills — comfortable building and interpreting revenue models, royalty structures, and ROI/breakeven analysis

  • Excellent relationship management and cross-cultural communication skills, given the global and multi-region nature of the ASP network

  • Proficiency with Excel/spreadsheet-based analysis tools; experience with CRM or partner management platforms a plus

Preferred:

  • Experience with biomedical test equipment, calibration standards (ISO 17025), or quality systems (ISO 9001/13485)

  • Experience running or participating in Kaizen / continuous-improvement events

  • Prior experience managing international distributor, dealer, or service-partner networks

  • Familiarity with royalty or licensing-based partner compensation models

About the Leaving Violence Program
Telstra Health proudly delivers the Leaving Violence Program, a national service supporting victim-survivors taking steps to leave violent relationships and establish lives free from violence.

Through practical support and financial assistance, the program helps eligible individuals move towards greater safety and independence at a critical point in their lives.

As a Support Officer in the Leaving Violence Program, you’ll be a key point of contact for victim-survivors accessing the service. Working in a fast-paced, high-volume contact centre environment, you’ll provide responsive and empathetic support via phone and digital channels.

Overview

Description

The Service Desk Analyst (SDA) will support MRO’s internal employee base and external customers with technical assistance, administration, configuration, and provisioning of hardware and software across our internal systems and healthcare products. The SDA is a “Tier 1” resource and is envisioned for a new or emerging professional with 1-5 years of existing experience and a broad interest in technology platforms. The SDA’s primary functions, detailed below, include handling a broad scope of end-user and customer support tickets, including intake of issues into our JIRA Service Management Platform, identity management functions, device troubleshooting, and support of our proprietary healthcare applications.

Responsibilities

Major Responsibilities:

  • End-User Support Ticketing: The SDA role will receive items submitted via our internal employees and external customers via our JIRA Service Management support portals and via telephone intake. Responsibilities include adequately identifying and classifying the issue (“ticket coding”), performing best steps to resolve using existing knowledge and/or documentation, and either resolving or escalating the issue to our “Tier 2” Support teams. Maintaining thorough, accurate, and timely ticket updates to reporters is essential.
  • User Management: The SDA will frequently utilize a suite of technology platforms related to user management functions, including AD Manager, Entra ID, and our suite of proprietary healthcare applications. Typical activities involve administrative requests to add, remove, or modify access. Some activities require additional approval from parties within and outside of the Support organization.
  • Troubleshooting and Remote Resolution: The SDA role is the first resolving party for the MRO technology organization and is a critical component to ensuring trouble tickets are closed promptly, accurately, and professionally for both internal employees and external customers. The SDA will utilize remote access tools to remotely connect and resolve issues reported or engage in direct phone calls or scheduled support sessions with issue reporters. While the primary goal is always to work to resolve an issue, the Service Desk is a fast-paced and high-volume team that requires individuals capable of differentiating between resolvable issues and those that would be better escalated. Excellent attention to detail and notetaking within the ticket is required to make the escalation process easier for both our internal team members and customers.
  • Onboarding and Offboarding: The SDA role is vital to our employee lifecycle activities and is the responsible entity for ensuring that new MRO team members are provisioned the proper user accounts and access prior to their start date and terminated team members’ accounts are terminated within our agreed timeframes to comply with internal and external regulations. The SDA role works with partners in Desktop Support and a third-party provisioning entity to facilitate the delivery of required hardware to new hires as well as a collection mechanism for retrieving hardware from terminated team members.

Engagement type: Independent consultant, 1099 hourly.

A great proposal is the difference between a captured opportunity and an awarded contract. We have the capture motion ramping up. What is already built

The Wilkinson Firm is a workforce strategy and staffing firm headquartered across NC and Atlanta. We launched in April 2025 and are now in Year 2 of operations. Two operational divisions today (HR Advisory for the mental health industry, Premium Hospitality and Event Staffing). Government Contracting division being formally stood up this quarter. Three active staffing contracts in delivery. FY26 trajectory $425-525K. Zero loans, zero institutional debt.

Bench credentials: Former EEOC Administrative Law Judge, employment attorneys (JD, MBA), clinical advisors, 32-year enterprise operations specialist. 47 combined years HHS experience.

Engagement is hourly. Per-proposal scope and budget defined at proposal kickoff. Win-based bonus stack negotiable on top of hourly rate for proposals that result in awarded contracts.

What we believe

Trust before revenue. Mission before money. Real seats, real upside. We build durable federal relationships through earned credibility. We win together. We pay people in real numbers, not pizza parties.

jobs.excerpt: Our MissionOur mission is to SAVE AND IMPROVE LIVES BY EMPOWERING HEALTHCARE CONSUMERS.
jobs.description:
Our Mission

Our mission is to SAVE AND IMPROVE LIVES BY EMPOWERING HEALTHCARE CONSUMERS. Come be part of remarkable.

Overview

How You Can Make a Difference

The AVP, Identity & Access Management, the enterprise authority on identity — the architect, evangelist, and operational owner of an identity-first security model in which identity is the control plane for a cloud-first, zero trust enterprise.

This leader defines and executes a multi-year B2E IAM strategy spanning identity governance and administration (IGA), privileged access management (PAM), customer and workforce access management, non-human/machine identity, and identity threat detection and response (ITDR), and is accountable for the engineering rigor, control effectiveness, and audit posture of the entire identity fabric.

This is a role for a practitioner-leader and recognized thought leader: someone who has designed and operated identity programs at scale, who is fluent in modern identity standards and protocols (OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML 2.0, SCIM, FIDO2/WebAuthn), who can whiteboard an authorization model one hour and defend a control posture to auditors and executives the next, and who actively shapes the direction of the identity discipline — inside the organization and in the broader industry — through published points of view, standards engagement, and community leadership.

What You’ll be Doing

  • Identity Strategy & Thought Leadership:
    • Own and evangelize a multi-year AI led identity strategy and reference architecture that treats identity as the primary security perimeter, aligned to zero trust principles (NIST SP 800-207) and enterprise business objectives.
    • Serve as the organization's most senior voice on identity: publish internal position papers and architectural decision records, brief executive leadership and the Board on identity risk, and represent the company externally through industry forums, standards bodies, conference speaking, and peer communities.
    • Anticipate and translate emerging shifts — decentralized identity, verifiable credentials, passwordless/phishing-resistant authentication, AI-agent and workload identity, continuous access evaluation (CAEP/Shared Signals) — into pragmatic roadmap decisions with clear build/buy/retire rationale.
  • Organizational Leadership:
    • Build, lead, and mentor a high-performing team of IAM architects, engineers, and analysts; establish engineering career paths, on-call/operational maturity, and a culture of automation-first identity operations.
    • Operate identity as a product: define OKRs and SLOs for a prioritized stakeholder backlog. Own the cycle time and unit cost of identity operations and publish a quarterly efficiency target.
    • Drive hyper-automation of access operations: zero-touch joiner, mover and leaver, self-service access with policy-driven approvals, and a measurable, sustained reduction in manual access tickets and handle time.
  • Identity Governance & Administration (IGA):
    • Architect and operate the full identity lifecycle — joiner/mover/leaver (JML) automation driven by authoritative HR sources, birthright provisioning, SCIM-based downstream integration, and deprovisioning SLAs measured in minutes to hours.
    • Design and mature the enterprise access model using Agentic AI capabilities: role engineering and role mining, RBAC evolving toward attribute- and policy-based access control (ABAC/PBAC), segregation-of-duties (SoD) rulesets, and risk-based, evidence-quality access certifications that eliminate rubber-stamping.
    • Own governance of entitlement sprawl across SaaS, IaaS, and on-prem estates, including cloud infrastructure entitlement management (CIEM) and least-privilege enforcement in AWS/Azure environments.
  • Authentication, Authorization & Directory Architecture:
    • Set the enterprise standard for authentication: phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn), passwordless adoption, adaptive/risk-based authentication, and session management policies calibrated to data sensitivity.
    • Own federation and SSO architecture (SAML 2.0, OIDC/OAuth 2.0), token security and lifetime strategy, and conditional access policy design across the enterprise application portfolio.
    • Govern directory and identity-store architecture — Entra ID and Active Directory hardening (tiered administration, attack-path reduction), hybrid identity synchronization, and rationalization of legacy identity repositories.
    • Advance externalized, policy-as-code authorization patterns (e.g., OPA/Rego, Cedar) for fine-grained, auditable access decisions in modern applications.
  • Privileged Access & Non-Human Identity:
    • Own the privileged access management program: credential vaulting, session isolation and recording, just-in-time/zero-standing-privilege elevation, and break-glass governance.
    • Establish lifecycle governance for non-human identities — service accounts, API keys, certificates, workload identities, and emerging AI-agent identities — including inventory, ownership attestation, secrets management, and automated rotation.
  • IAM Platform Engineering & Operations:
    • Lead evaluation, selection, and engineering of the IAM technology stack — IGA, access management/IdP, PAM, CIEM, and ITDR platforms — with a bias toward API-first integration, infrastructure-as-code deployment, and CI/CD-managed identity configuration.
    • Ensure availability, resilience, and disaster recovery of identity services as tier-zero infrastructure; identity outages are business outages.
    • Instrument the identity fabric end to end: stream identity telemetry to SIEM, define detections for identity-centric attack techniques (credential stuffing, token theft, MFA fatigue, golden ticket/SAML forging, privilege escalation), and partner with the SOC on ITDR playbooks.
    • Deliver agentic identity operations partnering closely with HealthEquity's in-house AI teams. This includes AI agents for access request triage, certification review, entitlement clean-up and anomaly-driven revocation.
  • Risk, Compliance & Assurance:
    • Own identity-related control design and operating effectiveness for HIPAA Security Rule safeguards, HITRUST CSF, SOC 1/SOC 2, SOX ITGCs, and applicable state privacy regimes; serve as primary identity interface for internal audit, external auditors, and regulators.
    • Run a continuous identity risk program: access-risk scoring, toxic-combination detection, periodic attack-path and privilege-escalation reviews, and identity-specific tabletop exercises.
    • Develop and maintain incident response plans for identity compromise scenarios and lead identity workstreams during security incidents.

What You’ll Need to be Successful

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related discipline, or equivalent work experience. Master's degree preferred.
  • 12–15+ years of progressive information security experience
  • Demonstrated track record of architecting and delivering at least one major identity transformation end to end,(e.g., IGA platform implementation, workforce IdP migration, PAM program build-out, zero trust identity modernization, or large-scale consumer identity modernization).

Specialized Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Deep, hands-on-credible expertise across the identity domain: IGA, access management, PAM, CIEM, ITDR, directory services, and non-human identity.
  • Fluency in identity standards and protocols — OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML 2.0, SCIM, LDAP/Kerberos, FIDO2/WebAuthn — and the architectural trade-offs among them.
  • Enterprise experience with leading IAM platforms (e.g., SailPoint, Saviynt, Okta, Microsoft Entra, Ping Identity, CyberArk, Delinea or comparable) and with integrating identity into SIEM/SOAR ecosystems.
  • Working knowledge of zero trust architecture (NIST SP 800-207), NIST SP 800-63 digital identity guidelines, and least-privilege design in cloud environments (AWS IAM, Azure RBAC/Entra).
  • Strong command of identity-relevant regulatory and assurance frameworks — HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2, SOX ITGCs — and experience defending control design to auditors.
  • Evidence of thought leadership: published writing, conference talks, standards or working-group participation, patents, open-source contribution, or recognized community leadership in the identity space.
  • Executive-caliber communication — able to translate deep technical architecture into board-level risk narratives — paired with strong leadership, mentorship, and team-building skills.
  • Experience running identity operations at scale with automation, orchestration and AI or agentic tooling; consumer identity (CIAM) experience is a plus.

Certifications, Licenses, Registrations

  • Relevant industry certifications strongly preferred — e.g., CISSP, CISM, CISA, CIDPRO, or vendor-specific identity certifications (SailPoint, Okta, Microsoft, CyberArk).

Travel Requirements

  • Occasional travel to attend training, industry conferences, or meetings may be required.

This is a remote position.

ABOUT UNRAVEL CARBON

Unravel Carbon is an enterprise software that helps companies track and reduce their carbon emissions, focusing on Asia, based in Singapore.

It is the first AI-powered decarbonization platform in Asia that converts any company's accounting data into full supply chain carbon data in seconds, generates climate solutions automatically and auto-populates regulatory disclosure reports.

We aim to accelerate the participation of all companies, big and small, in the global fight against climate change. And we want to do it the 21st century way—autonomous, painless, and beautiful.

Unravel consists of a team of software engineers, data scientists, founders and climate experts with a passion to solve the world's most pressing issue—climate change. Collectively, our leadership team has launched and invested in multiple companies, and are now combining their experience and knowledge here at Unravel.

We are backed by some of the world's best funds and investors such as Y Combinator, Sequoia.

Unravel was founded in Q4/2021 with headquarters in Singapore.

ABOUT THE ROLE

This role is dedicated to expanding Unravel Carbon's partner base in Japan; identifying, recruiting and formalising relationships with resellers, consultancies that can extend our commercial reach well beyond what is direct.

As Account Executive you will own the full partner lifecycle, from researching the landscape and approaching the right firms, Onboarding and enabling partners. You understand how indirect sales motion works, you know how to build trust, relationship at Partner level, and you are energized for creating a network of companies that sell on our behalf.

This is a strategic role with real ownership. You will shape Unravel Carbon's partner programme in Japan from the ground up, define the ideal partner profile and build the infrastructure onboarding process, joint business plans, enablement materials that makes the broader Japan commercial motion scale. You will report to the Japan Country Manager and contribute insights to Unravel Carbon's growth.

​

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Partner Identification: Research and map Japan's potential partner landscape, management consultancies, system integrators, ESG advisory firms, Sustainability adjacent technology resellers. Prioritise and approach high-potential partner candidates aligned with Unravel Carbon's target customer profiles and verticals.Lead partnership pitches, commercial negotiations, and contract execution with prospective partner organizations.Maintain a partner pipeline with full visibility into Partner recruitment stages, onboarding, timeline and activation status.
  • Partner Onboarding & Enablement : Design and deliver structured onboarding programmes for new partners - product demonstrations, Co-create joint business plans, aligning revenue targets, and co-marketing activities.Develop Japan localised sales collateral and demo guides that enable partners to sell Unravel Carbon independently, Develop and deliver sales and product training for Japan based implementation partners so they can confidently position and demo Unravel Carbon platform independently.
  • Account Expansion with Partners: Work side-by-side with partners on their existing Unravel Carbon accounts to identify and close upsell and cross-sell opportunities

​

ABOUT YOU

4+ years with experiences similar to being a quota carrying sales representative in an Enterprise Saas organisation or selling/consulting in the sustainability domain with a track record of excelling, bonus experience with the business development/partnerships.

Excited and motivated by a new challenge and see the potential for growth of Unravel Carbon in Japan

  • Willingness to do what it takes and roll-up your sleeve
  • High level of perseverance and tenacity; can push through objections to find novel and creative ways to connect with target enterprises
  • Aptitude to work with complex domain heavy enterprise SaaS products
  • Sales management experience to continue growing the future Japan team
  • Native-level Japanese with working fluency in English
  • Passion and interest in sustainability and combating climate change
  • Proven track record of building and activating reseller or channel partner network from scratch
  • Deep understanding of how indirect sales motion works in the Japanese enterprise market.
  • Strong commercial acumen with experience structuring and negotiating partnership agreements.

​

YOUR WORK STYLE

  • Focused and driven - achieving your objectives is critical to you
  • Proposition-minded, communicating ideas in a sales and customer-centric way
  • Analytical and detail-oriented, and fully capable of navigating and combining various data points to pull out key insights to generate and execute action plans
  • Self-starter (proactive and independent) with an ability to prioritise different assignments and tasks to meet deadlines
  • Comfortable working in a collaborative environment
  • Eager to think outside of the box and creatively problem-solve
  • Familiarity with GHG protocol, TCFD or corporate sustainability

​

YOUR PREFERRED BACKGROUND

A bachelor's degree (or a post-degree diploma) in business/economics, sustainability, with working experience in a related Sales / Business Development role.

WHAT WE OFFER YOU

The opportunity to get in at the early stage of our market expansion and to shape what Unravel Carbon is for the Japanese market.

We offer an exciting challenge for a purpose-driven person who thoroughly enjoys learning and takes ownership in a multicultural, semi- virtual, and pioneering organisation.

We nurture a culture that allows you to thrive, where your skills can be honed, and your ideas will be heard, and where collaboration across teams and with global partners is the default.

At Unravel Carbon, we are committed to cultivating a workplace that celebrates and values diversity, promotes equity, and ensures inclusion for all employees. Our commitment to DEI is foundational to our culture, guiding our actions, policies, and practices. We are committed to implement unbiased recruitment strategies, diverse candidate sourcing, and inclusive hiring practices to attract and retain talent from varied backgrounds.

​

BENEFITS

Complete social insurance (health, employee pension, employment, workers' compensation)

This role is responsible for developing and maintaining Smartsheet reports and dashboards, Power BI reporting solutions, portfolio KPIs, governance reporting, and executive-level report-outs used in weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual business reviews. This role combines analytical expertise, data visualization, portfolio management knowledge, and executive communication skills to transform project and portfolio data into actionable insights that support organizational strategy and operational excellence.

Job Title: Senior Director, R&D Capability Enablement

Job Location: Ontario, Canada

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

Senior Director, R&D Capability Enablement

What you will do


Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role you will translate R&D strategy into learning experiences, role readiness, and development opportunities that build workforce capability across R&D. In partnership with R&D leaders and functional learning partners, the role defines how priority capabilities are built, designs the experiences that enable them, and prepares employees to perform successfully. 

Working with R&D leaders and subject matter experts, the Senior Director translates business priorities into learning experiences and content that is accurate, useful, and easy to find. The role leads instructional designers, establishes content creation standards and a content management strategy, and uses learning analytics to show leaders what is working, where capability gaps remain, and where to focus investment. 


What we expect of you

We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The professional we seek is a person with these qualifications.


Key Responsibilities

Capability Strategy & Needs 

  • Partner with R&D leaders to identify current and emerging capability needs tied to scientific priorities, operating plans, and workforce plans. 
  • Use colleague feedback, capability assessments, performance data, and business priorities to identify gaps and sequence learning investments. 
  • Maintain a rolling capability roadmap and review it with R&D leadership at least twice a year. 

Learning Experience & Instructional Design Leadership 

  • Lead and develop instructional designers, set portfolio priorities, allocate work, and coach the team on learning design and delivery. 
  • Design role-based learning journeys and pathways, using a 70/20/10 approach where appropriate and drawing on instructor-led, digital, experiential, and coached learning. 
  • Create curricula and end-to-end learning experiences for priority capabilities, including instructional design, content development, and facilitation in partnership with subject matter experts. 

R&D Capability Architecture & Framework 

  • Translate leadership-defined R&D priorities into a shared capability architecture and framework, including core capabilities and proficiency expectations. 
  • Partner with leaders across R&D functions, including clinical development, data science, translational science, and research, to align priorities and provide guidance on competencies for critical roles. 
  • Translate the framework into role-based learning architecture, journeys, pathways, and manager resources that functions can use in their day-to-day work. 
  • Use feedback from learners and leaders, along with capability data, to update the framework as R&D needs change. 

Performance Readiness 

  • Oversee training governance, training management, and assignment processes for learning owned by Capability Enablement, with clear roles and standards. 
  • Develop end-to-end process learning for priority R&D workflows, partnering with process owners and functional teams on local learning needs. 
  • Define readiness expectations for priority functions and critical roles, and use appropriate checks to understand whether employees can perform required work. 

Advanced Capability Programs 

  • Design targeted programs for future-potential and high-potential R&D talent, including internships, rotations, mentorship, and focused development opportunities. 
  • Develop capability academies for priority R&D needs, such as AI application, when they address a defined business need. 
  • Focus these programs on targeted capability acceleration that complements Enterprise talent development and avoids duplicating existing programs. 

Learning Analytics & Business Impact 

  • Define measures for each learning goal, including reach, engagement, capability gains, application on the job, and relevant business outcomes. 
  • Create clear dashboards and reports so leaders can see participation, capability progress, persistent gaps, and trends across learning programs. 
  • Evaluate learning investments with appropriate assessments and business measures, explain the findings and their limits, and help leaders make informed prioritization and resourcing decisions. 

Content Standards & Management Strategy 

  • Set standards for learning content creation, including clear objectives, instructional design quality, accessibility, scientific accuracy, and subject matter review. 
  • Define a content management strategy for taxonomy, ownership, version control, discoverability, review cadence, archiving, and retirement. 
  • Maintain a curated R&D learning catalog and guide build, buy, reuse, and retirement decisions to reduce duplication and keep resources current. 

Operating Model & Functional Learning Partnership 

  • Design a learning operating model with clear governance, decision rights, service expectations, and ownership across central and functional teams. 
  • Partner with each R&D function to tailor enterprise capability builds to local needs through business consulting, prioritized capability builds, and critical-role consultation. 
  • Treat functional learning partnership as an operating approach, not a separate organization, and clarify ownership with R&D functions and Enterprise partners. 
  • Keep Capability Enablement focused on shared capability strategy, priority learning architecture and experiences, and common standards; functional teams retain ownership of local learning needs and process-specific education.
  • Do not own function-specific competency models for every role, all process learning across R&D, Quality-owned GxP training, employee performance management, or programs that duplicate Enterprise offerings.
  • Present capability and learning analytics to R&D leaders, connecting results to decisions about priorities and investment.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree and 10+ years in learning and development or a related field 
  • Strong expertise in adult learning, instructional design, performance consulting, and digital learning ecosystems. 
  • Experience designing and scaling enterprises or function-wide capability strategies 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 10 years in learning, capability, or organizational development, with significant time inside pharma/biotech R&D. 
  • Demonstrated experience designing, owning, or scaling a capability framework across multiple functions. 
  • Experience leading instructional designers or learning design teams and overseeing the quality of a broad learning portfolio. 
  • Experience designing role-based learning journeys, curricula, academies, or development programs for priority capabilities.
  • Experience establishing learning content standards, governance, or a content management strategy. 
  • Experience using learning analytics and evaluation to guide decisions and communicate learning impact to leaders. 
  • Executive-level stakeholder management and comfort presenting learning strategy and findings to senior R&D leaders. 
  • Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree in a relevant field (organizational psychology, science, or related) preferred. 

Core Competencies 

  • Capability strategy and foresight — connects R&D priorities to current and emerging capability needs. 
  • Instructional design leadership — sets direction, develops designers, and maintains quality across the learning portfolio. 
  • Content strategy and governance — establishes clear creation standards and manages content across its lifecycle. 
  • Learning analytics and impact — interprets evidence and helps leaders use it to guide priorities and investment. 
  • Systems thinking and cross-functional alignment — builds shared approaches that work across R&D functions. 
  • Executive influence and business orientation — connects learning decisions to R&D priorities and outcomes. 

What you can expect of us

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.


The salary range for the position is $192,525 - $260,475 CAD.

Senior Full Stack Developer

Blurb.fm · Remote (Canada) · Full-Time

THE COMPANY

Who We Are

Blurb builds revenue-generating content products for the most influential media companies in the world. We scale content from what already exists — turning catalogs and brand assets into high performing formats for every major platform.

Our mission is simple: help media companies unlock growth through high volume, high impact content.

THE TEAM

How We Work

We are a nimble, execution obsessed team of engineers who thrive on solving real business problems with smart, scalable solutions. Engineering at Blurb is about building the backbone that powers performant content systems for our clients, not writing speculative code.

We are a small, high trust team. There is no handoff culture here. Every engineer scopes, architects, builds and ships. You will work closely with designers, product, and creative leads and you will own your work end to end.

We care about impact, not just implementation. We engineer with speed, stability and long term adaptability in mind.

THE ROLE

What You Will Do

As a Senior Full Stack Developer, you will be a core contributor to the platform that makes content at scale possible. You will architect, build and maintain systems that handle high volume video and content workflows for major media clients.

This is a senior individual contributor (IC) role. You will not be managing or delegating, you will be doing. Priority is execution.

In your first 30–60 days

  • Work closely with the team to deeply understand our products, APIs, and infrastructure.

  • Get comfortable in the codebases by shipping bug fixes and small features.

  • Begin identifying areas of improvement in architecture, developer experience, or tooling.

Once you are fully ramped

  • Architect new products and features with stability, flexibility and performance in mind.

  • Own large scale efforts from technical scoping through to production delivery.

  • Lead the development of new tools and production pipelines.

  • Maintain and evolve infrastructure proactively, not just reactively.

  • Ensure quality of all deliverables. Set the bar, then hold it.

  • Contribute ideas that improve how we build and what we build.

This role is NOT right for you if

  • Your best work is coordinating and delegating rather than writing code.

  • You prefer a structured corporate environment with established processes and a full team around you.

  • You expect someone else to resolve ambiguity before you can move.

  • You rely on AI to produce code you do not fully understand or cannot defend.

This is a builder role. You will write code every single day.

﻿

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Hard Skills

  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, with meaningful back-end or full-stack ownership.

  • Strong, production-grade TypeScript (Node.js) — this is a core requirement, not a nice-to-have.

  • Solid Python skills, especially for data-heavy or ML-adjacent work.

  • Hands-on experience with Google Cloud Services (Firebase/Firestore, Cloud Functions, Cloud Run, Compute Engine).

  • Proven ability to own the full product lifecycle: architecture build delivery maintenance.

  • Experience designing and scaling systems for high-volume, performance-sensitive workloads.

  • Comfort working in a Linux environment; Bash/shell scripting is a regular part of the job.

How You Work

  • You thrive in ambiguity. You define requirements when they are unclear instead of waiting for them to be handed to you.

  • You are a self directed executor. You pick up tasks, figure them out and ship without needing to be unblocked at every step.

  • You are comfortable using AI as a productivity multiplier (Claude, ChatGPT, etc.) while maintaining your own critical thinking, you architect and analyze code yourself, you do not outsource it.

  • You communicate clearly and proactively across any medium, async messages, docs, code reviews or live calls.

  • You are an advocate for documentation and organized codebases, but pragmatic about what actually gets read and used.

  • You are adaptable. Priorities shift in a startup, you shift with them without losing momentum.

  • You have genuine curiosity about the work: side projects, new tools, emerging patterns in your domain.

Bonus points

  • Experience with video processing, media pipelines, or content-at-scale infrastructure.

  • Familiarity with PyTorch or TensorFlow for ML adjacent tasks.

  • Experience with Next.js, Tailwind CSS, or modern React patterns.

  • Prior startup experience — especially as a hands on IC in a small team.

  • Passion for the music or media industry.

THE STACK

Technologies You Will Work With

  • TypeScript (Node.js)
  • Python
  • Google Cloud Services
  • Firebase / Firestore
  • Cloud Functions / Cloud Run
  • Compute Engine
  • Next.js
  • Tailwind CSS
  • PyTorch / TensorFlow
  • Linux
  • Bash / Shell Scripting
  • Adobe After Effects

LIFE AT BLURB

What to Expect

  • Fully remote. We are a distributed team and have been from the start. We have an office in Calgary where you can use.

  • High ownership, low bureaucracy. You will have real influence over how we build and what we build.

  • A small, senior team. No layers, your work ships directly to production and to clients.

  • Fast moving environment. We iterate quickly and expect the same from the people we hire.

We move quickly when we find someone great. If this sounds like the right environment for you, we'd love to hear from you.

  • Identify operational risks, recurring issues, process gaps, and opportunities to improve quality, efficiency, reporting, and customer service.

Federal and Local Occupational Safety and Health Regulations

Industry Consensus Standards

Circet USA Injury and Illness Prevention Program Manual

Relevant experience should include Joint Pole Association (JPA), Joint Pole Committee (JPC), utility, pole attachment, wireless telecommunications, or related infrastructure programs. A minimum of two years of project management, team leadership, or supervisory experience is preferred.
  • Working knowledge of JPA/JPC processes, pole attachment requirements, utility coordination, field inspection activities, milestone tracking, denials, contested transactions, and supporting documentation.
  • Experience managing field personnel, vendors, subcontractors, or multi-functional project teams and holding resources accountable for productivity, quality, schedule, and customer requirements.
  • Demonstrated ability to interpret contracts, customer requirements, utility/JPA documentation, billing requirements, technical records, and related project documentation.

  • Demonstrated ability to manage and interface with customers, utilities, Joint Pole Associations/Committees, field personnel, project teams, and other internal and external stakeholders.

Monitors process, progress, and results with a focus on final resolution. Influences and navigates the organization to ensure completion.

SUMMARY:

We are seeking an experienced Strategic Sourcing Manager to lead sourcing, supplier management, and contract negotiations across technology and professional services categories for a temporary staffing and workforce solutions organization. This role will be responsible for developing sourcing strategies, optimizing supplier performance, negotiating favorable commercial terms, and driving cost savings while ensuring quality, compliance, and business continuity.

The ideal candidate combines strong procurement expertise with exceptional stakeholder management skills and experience managing complex supplier relationships in technology, consulting, professional services, and contingent workforce environments.

Location: Remote (West Coast candidates preferred)

ESSENTIAL DUTIES and RESPONSIBILITIES:

Strategic Sourcing & Category Management

  • Develop and execute sourcing strategies for technology and professional services spend categories, including software, SaaS, IT services, consulting, managed services, telecommunications, and business services.
  • Conduct spend analysis, market research, and supplier assessments to identify sourcing opportunities and cost optimization initiatives.
  • Lead competitive sourcing events, including RFIs, RFPs, RFQs, and supplier evaluations.
  • Build category strategies that align with organizational goals, operational requirements, and growth objectives.

Supplier Relationship Management

  • Establish and maintain strong relationships with strategic suppliers and service providers.
  • Evaluate supplier performance through defined KPIs, scorecards, and business reviews.

Contract Negotiation & Management

  • Lead commercial negotiations for supplier agreements, statements of work, master service agreements, software licensing agreements, and professional services contracts.

  • Partner with legal, finance, IT, and business stakeholders throughout the contracting lifecycle.

Stakeholder Partnership

  • Collaborate with department leaders to understand business requirements and sourcing needs.
  • Provide procurement guidance and recommendations to internal stakeholders.
  • Support budgeting, forecasting, and vendor selection decisions.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor on sourcing best practices and supplier management strategies.

Cost Savings & Value Creation

  • Track sourcing project outcomes and report savings achievements.
  • Drive process improvements that increase procurement efficiency and supplier effectiveness.

EDUCATION and EXPERIENCE:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain Management, Finance, Procurement, or related field.

CORE KNOWLEDGE and SKILLS:

  • Ability to effectively communicate and influence key stakeholders to support proposed strategies, process improvements and operational decisions.

  • Strong multi-tasker with ability to prioritize and adapt fast in an ever-changing environment
  • Effectively manage numerous projects at a given time in a fast-paced environment
  • Ability to think creatively, work independently and as part of a team to solve problems given limited resources and time and, have a strong work ethic, and adhere to deadlines.
  • Solid organizational and project management skills
  • Results oriented
  • Ability to effectively interact and communicate with all levels of management to build partnerships with various departments and suppliers
  • Experience performing cost savings analysis using advanced Excel including V-look ups, pivot tables, and other related software applications
  • Experience with procurement, contract lifecycle management, or spend analytics systems (Oracle Fusion).

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:

This position will not have any direct supervisory responsibilities.

Salary Range: $124,300 – $155,300 annually, depending on experience and geographic location plus eligibility for an annual bonus, subject to plan terms.

Please note that actual compensation offered may vary based on local pay requirements, and will meet or exceed state-specific minimum wage or salary thresholds.

  • Proven experience with TPM/TPO solutions—either as a system administrator, domain expert, or having played an integral role in a TPM system implementation or deployment.
  • Advanced consultative selling expertise—ability to diagnose complex business challenges, understand client pain points, and translate them into compelling ROI-driven solution narratives that demonstrate competitive advantage.
  • Demonstrated ability to deliver clear, concise, and impactful product demonstrations and presentations that effectively communicate functionality, value proposition, and competitive differentiation to both technical and business stakeholders; comfort presenting to executive audiences.

jobs.description:
The Wilkinson Firm (TWF) is an enterprise workforce strategy and solutions company with two divisions: HR Advisory (behavioral health and HHS focus) and Hospitality Staffing. Headquartered in NC and Atlanta, Georgia, respectively. The next 24 months are about building and expanding a real book across the HR Advisory practice serving behavioral health and HHS clients.

About this role

TWF's HR Advisory division has product-market fit and a founding-cohort partnership pipeline. The closing motion has been founder-led until now. You're the first SDR. You'll build the outbound motion that refills the pipeline at the cadence the division needs to hit $1.2M Y1 ARR. If you're the right person, you become a partner in this division long-term.

The partner upside

  • TWF Earned Equity Ladder: Tier 2 (1-3% equity) eligible at month 6 against the 5-gate evaluation
  • Tier 3 (3-8% equity) progression by month 18 if you continue performing and take on strategic ownership
  • Tier 4 (8-15% equity, true partner level) by month 36 for the right person
  • HR Advisory engagements are bigger-ticket than Hospitality Staffing. Your commission share compounds faster per signed deal
  • The math: 8-15 signed engagements in Y1 at $40,000 to $80,000 average annualized retainer puts the division near its ARR target and puts you in Tier 2 equity range by month 6

The pay

  • Base: $0 first 90 days. Modest base ($1,500 to $2,500/month) introduced at month 4 once you've sourced 2-3 signed engagements and cash flow supports it
  • Commission: 10% of first-year contract value on every signed HR Advisory engagement you sourced
  • Bonus stack: $250 per qualified Discovery Call that converts to a proposal, $2,500 per signed HR Advisory engagement, $1,000 per completed Workup
  • Realistic Y1 total comp at target performance: $45,000 to $115,000
  • Equity: see "The partner upside" above

What this is and isn't

This is:

  • Employee-level-1 on the outbound side of a relationship-led, advisory-grade services practice
  • Founder-led with hands-on weekly support during ramp
  • Equity-bearing with a real path to partner-level ownership
  • Built around relationships and trust. We close clinical executives by sitting in their world, not pitching at them

This isn't:

  • A mature SDR org with a playbook, dashboards, and an SDR manager above you. You'll help build them
  • A high-volume cold-spam motion. HHS executives screen out vendor-feeling outreach in two seconds
  • A hand-holding environment. People who need a defined system to operate inside will struggle here

What you'll do

  • Build the outbound playbook for behavioral health and HHS practice clients
  • Run 30-50 personally-signed cold emails per business day into Executive Directors, Practice Owners, Clinical Directors, CHROs, and CFOs
  • Send 25-40 LinkedIn Sales Navigator connection requests per week with one-line personalized opens
  • Place 8-15 warm-then-cold dials per day to people who opened or accepted
  • Lead with The Workup as the wedge offer in your outreach
  • Qualify replies, book Discovery Calls on the founder's calendar, log everything in HubSpot
  • Iterate copy weekly. Document what works so the next SDR has a playbook

Why this role exists

TWF's HR Advisory division has the founder closing, the Director of Community Partnerships sourcing warm relationships, and the partnership pipeline showing strong proof-points. There is no dedicated outbound motion to fill the rest of the funnel. You're it. Without you, the division can't hit its $1.2M Y1 ARR target. With you, it becomes the firm's flagship practice.

What success looks like

  • Day 30: outbound stack stood up, first 100 personally-signed emails sent, first 3 Discovery Calls booked, first Workup in flight
  • Day 60: 8-12 HR Advisory Discovery Calls booked per month becoming routine
  • Day 90: 10% positive reply rate sustained, first 1-2 signed engagements or strong proposal pipeline
  • Day 180: Tier 2 equity grant landed if performance sustained
  • Day 365: SDR playbook documented, contribution to $1.2M Y1 ARR target traceable in HubSpot, Tier 3 equity progression on the table

Who you are

  • 6 months to 3 years in B2B outbound sales (HR consulting, healthcare services, or PEO sales preferred)
  • Comfortable selling to mission-driven clinical executives who screen out vendor-feeling outreach
  • Familiar with behavioral health, IDD, or HHS sector, or willing to learn the vertical fast
  • You've worked in a startup or early-stage environment before, or you know that's the environment you want
  • You log every touch in CRM. If it's not logged, it didn't happen
  • Self-directed. The founder will not check your activity hourly
  • Eastern Time work hours

Bonus points

  • Prior experience at a behavioral health provider, IDD organization, or HHS-focused consultancy
  • Existing relationships with NABH, ABHW, or state-level behavioral health associations
  • SHRM credential or HR sector fluency
  • HubSpot, Apollo, or Sales Navigator fluency

How we work

  • Remote, Eastern Time
  • Async-friendly inside core hours (9am-1pm ET overlap minimum)
  • Weekly 1:1 with founder during ramp
  • Tech stack ready on Day 1: HubSpot, Apollo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Slack
  • You'll partner with the Account Executive (HR Advisory) on warm hand-offs and with the Director of Community Partnerships for context on the founding-cohort

What we believe

Trust before revenue. Mission before money. Long game. We treat every clinical executive like a peer, not a target. We build durable relationships, not flashy logos. We pay people in real upside, not in pizza parties.

Application Tips

  1. Visit . Five minutes. Understand the practice you'd be building with.
  2. Find The Wilkinson Firm on LinkedIn. Look around at our social media presence.
  3. In your cover note, tell us one thing: which behavioral health or HHS organization type would you target first, and why?

What to expect from us

  • Reply within 48 hours of application
  • First-round screen within 7 days
  • Full process: 2-3 weeks
  • We tell you yes or no. We do not ghost.

Our mission is to SAVE AND IMPROVE LIVES BY EMPOWERING HEALTHCARE CONSUMERS. Come be part of remarkable.

HealthEquity administers HSAs, FSAs, HRAs, COBRA, and commuter benefits, and our service operations exist to deliver a remarkable experience for our members. The Director, Demand Planning and Worforce Operations leads the consolidated Forecasting and Workforce Management pillar within the Workforce Strategy organization. This leader owns the end-to-end demand-to-delivery cycle: long-range and short-range demand forecasting, capacity and headcount planning, scheduling, and real-time operations across internal teams and BPO partner sites.

This is not a day-to-day execution role. The role is accountable for strategic direction, decision-ready insight for executives, capability-building across the team, and leading the organization through significant platform and operating-model change, including the Verint, Webex, and Amazon Connect migrations, and skill-based routing readiness.

What you will be doing

Forecasting and planning

  • Model and communicate expected outcomes, including service level, ASA, occupancy, and cost to serve, across scenarios; quantify risks and opportunities to support leadership decisions.

Workforce management operations

  • Direct scheduling, real-time queue management, and intraday performance across internal and outsourced sites, with tamper-clear audit of adherence and performance data.
  • Drive WFM platform modernization: Verint migration (scheduling, RTQM automation, outcome projection) and readiness for Webex and Amazon Connect capabilities.
  • Expand WFM scope beyond member and client services as automation matures.

The Opportunity

Fyfe's Power & Electrification Division partners with major energy developers and infrastructure clients to deliver large-scale renewable energy and power infrastructure projects across Australia. Based in the Philippines, you will work remotely as part of an integrated project team, contributing to greenfield developments and the upgrade and expansion of existing networks that support Australia's energy transition.

As a Senior Electrical Designer, you will play a key role in the design and delivery of Electrical Balance of Plant (EBOP) projects for wind farms, solar farms and BESS developments, while also supporting HV transmission and distribution infrastructure. You will collaborate virtually with experienced engineers and designers across Australia and the Philippines, gaining exposure to a broad range of technical disciplines and some of Australia's most significant energy projects.

This permanent work-from-home role offers exposure to HV substations, switchyards, underground and overhead reticulation systems, grid connection infrastructure and utility coordination activities. You will contribute to complex technical projects in a supportive team environment, with regular online collaboration across locations and time zones.

Please note: This position is open to candidates residing in the Philippines. The successful candidate will be employed locally through a third-party employment agency and will work exclusively with Fyfe's Power & Electrification Division.

The Impact You'll Have

  • Deliver high-quality electrical design documentation for HV substations, utility infrastructure and renewable energy projects.
  • Develop primary design deliverables including equipment layouts, cable routing, earthing systems, conduit layouts and detailed construction drawings.
  • Support the successful coordination and delivery of multidisciplinary design packages to meet project and client requirements.
  • Contribute to HV and LV power system designs, equipment selection and technical solutions for complex energy infrastructure projects.
  • Collaborate with engineers and project teams to enhance design quality, project delivery and technical outcomes.
  • Help shape the delivery of renewable energy, transmission and power infrastructure projects that support Australia's evolving energy sector.

What You'll Bring

We are looking for an experienced Senior Electrical Designer based in the Philippines who is comfortable working remotely with Australian project teams, solving complex technical challenges and delivering high-quality outcomes across a diverse portfolio.

  • A bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a closely related discipline from a recognised institution.
  • 8+ years' experience within a design consultancy environment.
  • Strong experience in HV substation design and detailed design delivery using MicroStation and AutoCAD.
  • Experience delivering electrical engineering designs across renewable energy, transmission, substations, power generation, hydrogen, oil & gas or related energy sectors.
  • Proven capability undertaking LV and HV power generation and distribution systems design, including equipment selection such as transformers, circuit breakers and associated electrical infrastructure.
  • Experience completing HV and LV power system studies including load flow, short circuit, cable sizing, arc flash, discrimination and protection, earthing and harmonics assessments.
  • Proficiency using electrical modelling software such as ETAP, EMTP or PSCAD.
  • Strong understanding of relevant Australian Standards, including AS 2067, IEEE 80, AS/NZS 1768, AS 3000, AS 3008, IEEE 1584 and NFPA 70.
  • Strong written and verbal English communication, organisational and problem-solving skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively in a remote, cross-border team.
  • Previous experience supporting Australian projects or working to Australian Standards is highly regarded.

It would be great if you also have experience in High Voltage and Low Voltage Switchboard design in accordance with AS 61439 and exposure to instrumentation and control systems.

Fyfe is an Australian multidisciplinary consultancy with more than 700 people across engineering, environment, planning and surveying. We partner with clients across the Energy & Resources and Property & Infrastructure sectors to deliver high-quality, commercially pragmatic solutions with a strong focus on client service and project delivery

Joining Fyfe from the Philippines means becoming a valued member of an international team, not an outsourced support function. Your expertise will have a genuine impact as you work on meaningful Australian energy projects and collaborate directly with experienced professionals across multiple disciplines.

jobs.excerpt: OverviewCherre is now a RealPage company, expanding our ability to deliver innovative data and technology solutions that transform the real estate industry.
jobs.description:
Overview

Cherre is now a RealPage company, expanding our ability to deliver innovative data and technology solutions that transform the real estate industry. Join us as we build what’s next together.

Cherre is the leading real estate data management and analytics platform. We connect, resolve, and organize the fragmented data real estate organizations rely on: internal systems, public records, and third-party providers, into a single, connected source of truth. Institutional investors, asset managers, and brokers use Cherre to power underwriting, portfolio management, and reporting on data they can trust.

Our work sits at the intersection of real estate domain knowledge and modern data infrastructure, and this role is central to how we translate that platform into value for our most strategic clients.

Responsibilities

We're looking for a Senior Director of Solutions Architecture to lead the domain-first solutions engine of our sales and delivery motion. You'll own the presales function end to end, from first discovery call through handoff into delivery. You'll manage and grow a team of Solution Architects and Business Analysts, and you'll set the vision for how we scope, demonstrate, and win.

This role rests first on deep real assets domain expertise, complemented by technical acumen and a strong market-facing presence. You'll be credible discussing property operations and investment strategy with a client's leadership, guiding the solution alongside their data and engineering teams, and representing Cherre in front of a prospect's decision-makers. Domain fluency is the foundation; the ideal candidate pairs it with enough technical depth and executive presence to carry a solution from discovery through the deal.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You'll be in the room for our most strategic deals, shaping how we translate complex prospect requirements into compelling, credible solutions. Just as important, you'll be expected to modernize how the function operates. We want a leader who builds tools and AI-assisted workflows that make the team faster and sharper, not one who simply runs the existing playbook.

  • Lead the domain engine. Understand each client’s business deeply and align solutions to achieve their objectives.
  • Lead the presales function. Own the full presales lifecycle and partner closely with Sales to drive technical wins on strategic and enterprise opportunities.
  • Manage and develop the team. Hire, coach, and grow a team of Solution Architects and Business Analysts. Set standards, build expertise, balance workloads across active deals, and foster a culture of technical rigor.
  • Drive scoping and discovery. Personally lead scoping and discovery for strategic prospects, uncovering requirements, identifying risks, and defining solutions that map to real business outcomes.
  • Own the RFP process. Run the RFP response process end to end, ensuring responses are accurate, differentiated, and delivered on time.
  • Ensure clean handoffs to Delivery. Build and maintain a repeatable bridge from presales scoping into implementation so nothing is lost between the sale and the build.
  • Modernize the function with AI. Design and build skills and agentic workflows, and optimize the agentic fleet to streamline the process from scoping through delivery. Continuously identify ways to use AI to improve the quality and speed of the team’s output.
  • Represent the point of view. Publish, speak, and advocate for Cherre’s perspective on real assets data and semantic infrastructure, shaping how the market thinks about the problem—not just how Cherre solves it.
  • Close the loop into Product. Translate market and client signals from the field into product roadmap input, ensuring the roadmap reflects what the market is actually telling you—not just what has already been scoped.

Qualifications

  • Real assets domain expertise spanning the full stack: up into the capital stack (fund structures, debt and equity vehicles, investment vehicles) and down into the physical, operational asset (property operations, leasing, maintenance, tenant and resident experience). A track record of scoping and designing solutions that hold together across both ends of that stack, not just one.
  • Global and cross-asset-class experience: comfortable moving between multifamily, office, industrial, retail, and alternative asset classes, and across US, European, and APAC market conventions and regulatory contexts.
  • 10+ years in real estate, proptech, or consulting, with experience leading teams of domain and technical experts.
  • Technical fluency across entity resolution, graph-based data models, and semantic layer architecture, sufficient to guide solution and demo design and engage credibly with a client's data and engineering teams on how identity, confidence, and lineage actually work under the platform, not just what the platform outputs.
  • Fluent in the shift from human-readable reporting to typed, governed interfaces built for agent consumption: why a report could tolerate semantic drift that an agent reasoning from the same data cannot, and why that difference is now a product architecture problem, not a documentation problem.
  • Demonstrated thought leadership: a track record of publishing or speaking on real assets, data, or investment strategy, not just executing someone else's narrative.
  • Executive presence to represent Cherre externally, lead the room in strategic deals, and translate technical complexity into business value for institutional buyers.
  • The ability to operate as both a player and a coach: both getting hands-on in deals, and effective at hiring, developing, and leading a high-performing team behind you.
  • An AI-forward mindset, with hands-on experience building tools, automations, or agentic workflows.

Nice to have experience with:

  • AI tools such as Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT
  • Building AI agents and agentic workflows
  • Interacting with Github
  • Experience with knowledge management tools such as Obsidian

jobs.excerpt: Engagement type: Independent consultant, 1099 hourly.
jobs.description:
Engagement type: Independent consultant, 1099 hourly.
Rate range: $100 - $500 per hour, based on experience and scope (three-tier band detailed below).
Time commitment: Part-time or fractional, scales with pipeline (typically 10-40 hrs/week).
Location: Remote with quarterly DC travel preferred.
Reports to: GovCon Division Lead.

A note from the founder

TWF has built the scaffolding for federal work. MBE certification, SAM.gov registration, two operational divisions ready to serve federal contracts, a credentialed bench, and signed commercial customers proving the operating model. What is missing is the capture function. This engagement is for the operator who knows how to walk a federal opportunity from first signal through awarded contract, and who wants to build that function inside a firm where it does not exist yet.

What is already built

The Wilkinson Firm is a workforce strategy and staffing firm headquartered across NC and Atlanta. We launched in April 2025 and are now in Year 2 of operations. Two operational divisions today (HR Advisory for the mental health industry, Premium Hospitality and Event Staffing). Government Contracting division being formally stood up this quarter. Three active staffing contracts in delivery. FY26 trajectory $425-525K. Zero loans, zero institutional debt. Defined path to $5M+ over the next 24 months.

Federal-relevant scaffolding:[- Two operational divisions ready to serve federal contracts in HHS-adjacent verticals (VA mental health programs, DoD behavioral health support, HHS workforce IDIQs) and hospitality (federal lodging, on-base food service, training facility F&B).

What you own

  • Federal opportunity identification and qualification across SAM.gov, GSA Schedules, agency forecasts, and prime/sub channels
  • Capture-to-proposal lifecycle: opportunity assessment, teaming strategy, technical and price strategy, color-team reviews, submission readiness
  • Capture playbook documentation: pursuit criteria, gate reviews, win themes, ghosting strategy, competitive analysis
  • Prime and sub partner relationships and government POC management
  • Set-aside strategy and certification work (8(a), HUBZone, WOSB, SDVOSB) in coordination with the GovCon Division Lead
  • Pipeline visibility and reporting to firm leadership
  • Coaching the Proposal Manager and Federal Account Executive seats as they come online

Engagement structure

Hourly consulting rate, three tiers calibrated to experience and scope:

  • Foundational ($100-200/hr): Capture managers with 5-8 years experience, ramping into a director role
  • Director ($200-350/hr): Established capture directors with documented win history on $1M+ contracts
  • Principal ($350-500/hr): Senior capture principals with multi-million-dollar award history and Tier 1 prime experience

Engagement is hourly. Time commitment scales with pipeline activity, typically 10-40 hours per week. Win-based bonus stack negotiable on top of hourly rate for awarded contracts the engagement materially drove.

Success milestones

  • Day 30: Capture playbook drafted. Pursuit gate criteria documented. Initial pipeline of 10+ qualified opportunities.
  • Day 90: 2-4 active captures in formal pursuit. First teaming agreements signed. Pipeline value $1M+.
  • Day 180: 2-4 proposals submitted. First award or shortlist position. Win rate baseline established.

Who you are

  • 7-15 years in federal capture, proposal management, or BD for small to mid-size GovCon firms
  • Documented track record capturing $1M+ federal contracts
  • Shipley-trained or equivalent. SAM.gov fluent. Comfortable with FAR/DFARS terminology
  • Familiar with small business set-asides and the certification lifecycle
  • Past performance citations in workforce, HHS-adjacent, hospitality, or staffing services preferred
  • Comfortable building a function from scratch inside a founder-led firm
  • Located in DC, NC, GA, or willing to travel to DC quarterly

Bonus points

  • Prior role at a Tier 1 GovCon prime or boutique capture firm
  • Existing relationships at DoD, VA, HHS, GSA, or DHS
  • APMP credential
  • Track record of managed HUBZone or 8(a) certifications

How we will get to know each other

  1. Initial 30-minute fit conversation with the GovCon Division Lead
  2. Working session: walk through a real federal opportunity or proposal scenario we are actively considering
  3. Reference checks (3+ professional references) and work history verification
  4. Engagement letter, scope of work, and rate confirmation
  5. Kickoff within 7 days of signed engagement

2-4 weeks first conversation to active engagement.

What we believe

Trust before revenue. Mission before money. Real seats, real upside. We build durable federal relationships through earned credibility. We win together. We pay people in real numbers, not pizza parties. We are building something great and we want partners who feel the same.

Application tips

  1. Visit , ,
  2. Find The Wilkinson Firm on LinkedIn
  3. In your cover note, answer two questions: (1) what kind of GovCon engagement model works best for you (project-based, retained hours, hybrid), and (2) one example of a federal pursuit, proposal, or account you would point to as your strongest reference work

What to expect from us

  • Reply within 48 hours
  • First-round conversation within 7 days of qualification
  • Full process: 2-4 weeks
  • We tell you yes or no. We do not ghost.

Overview

Empower AI is AI for government. Empower AI gives federal agency leaders the tools to elevate the potential of their workforce with a direct path for meaningful transformation.
